steps.title: Score sentiment by aspect
steps.where: the Cortex Code sidebar, with `da1_feedback_analysis` open
steps.prompt: In the open notebook da1_feedback_analysis, put each cell I ask for under its matching numbered heading. Under heading 1, add a SQL cell named aspect_sentiment that uses AI_SENTIMENT to score 5 rows of FEEDBACK_TEXT from BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_FEEDBACK overall and for the aspects speed, communication and fees. Run it and explain the output.
steps.expect: the cell's result shows an overall sentiment plus a separate one for each aspect (positive, negative, neutral, mixed or unknown)

steps.title: Enrich all feedback once
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named enrich that creates the table BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED from STG_FEEDBACK left-joined to STG_CUSTOMERS. Keep the feedback columns plus CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR and RM_NAME. Add SENTIMENT_SCORE from AI_SENTIMENT's overall sentiment (positive = 1, negative = -1, neutral or mixed = 0; don't use the legacy SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SENTIMENT, which is blocked on new accounts), SENTIMENT_LABEL (POSITIVE above 0.3, NEGATIVE below -0.3, otherwise NEUTRAL) and TOPIC_CATEGORY from AI_CLASSIFY into one of: Performance Issue, Service Quality, Technical Problem, Positive Experience, Feature Request. Then add a SQL cell named by_scheme showing average sentiment and % negative by PAYMENT_TYPE, and run both.
steps.expect: about 2,000 scored rows, every one with a topic, and a per-scheme summary. Score once, query many times.

steps.title: Find churn risk in plain English
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named churn_risk that uses AI_FILTER on BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED with exactly this question: 'Does the client in this feedback explicitly state that they will or may leave the bank, move their business to another bank, review other banking providers, or tender their banking? Complaints without a stated intention to leave do not count. Feedback: {0}'. Show customer, payment type and the first 120 characters of the feedback, grouped by distinct feedback text with a count. Run it.
steps.expect: a short list - three distinct churn statements (reviewing other providers, moving to another bank, tendering their banking) - found by meaning rather than keywords. Ordinary complaints about delays or outages are left out. That's the difference between AI_FILTER and a sentiment score. They all come from Logistics clients, which the next step explains

steps.title: Chart sentiment by sector
steps.body:
Now chart it with the built-in chart tool, no Python needed: under the `sector_trend` result select **Chart**, set **Chart type** to **Line chart**, **X axis** to **MONTH** (sort ascending), **Y axis** to **AVG_SENTIMENT**, and group by **CUSTOMER_SECTOR**. Logistics falls clearly over the last four months (the same clients who talk about leaving), while Pharmaceuticals improves; other sectors move around without a trend.
**Tip:** the result panel also has a **Quick insights** button that summarises a result in the UI. Try it on `sector_trend`.
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named sector_trend with one row per complete month and customer sector from BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED: MONTH, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, AVG_SENTIMENT and FEEDBACK_COUNT, excluding the current partial month. Run it and tell me which sectors are getting worse.
steps.expect: a result table with one row per month and sector

steps.title: Summarise complaint themes per RM
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named rm_themes that creates the table BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.RM_FEEDBACK_THEMES with one row per RM_NAME from the NEGATIVE rows of FEEDBACK_ENRICHED: NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK (count) and TOP_THEMES using AI_AGG with the instruction "You are briefing a corporate banking relationship manager. List the top 3 recurring complaint themes in this client feedback, each with a one-line recommended action. Be concise." Run it, then add a cell that selects from RM_FEEDBACK_THEMES and shows the results.
steps.expect: the table is created (the first cell only reports success); the second cell shows one row per RM with three themes and actions

steps.title: Draft a client reply
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named draft_reply that uses AI_COMPLETE to draft a short, professional reply from a UK corporate bank to the most negative item in FEEDBACK_ENRICHED: acknowledge the issue, avoid admitting liability and offer a follow-up call. Run it, then print the draft reply as plain text under the cell so it is easy to read.
steps.expect: a client-ready draft for a human to review. The notebook is now a complete, re-runnable analysis you could share or schedule.

modules.note: AI functions run inside Snowflake's security boundary - no data leaves the platform and nothing is vectorised or stored by the model.
modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE DA1: AI SQL ON CUSTOMER FEEDBACK   (~45 min)
-- Persona: Data Analyst
-- Question: "What are corporate clients actually complaining about, by
--            scheme and by relationship manager - without reading 2,000 comments?"
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql (for STG_* views), or DE1
-- All functions run inside Snowflake: no data leaves the platform, no model training.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BANKING_WH;
USE SCHEMA BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA1.1 Overall and aspect-based sentiment
-- AI_SENTIMENT scores the whole text and named aspects separately
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT LEFT(FEEDBACK_TEXT, 90) AS FEEDBACK,
       AI_SENTIMENT(FEEDBACK_TEXT, ['speed', 'communication', 'fees']) AS ASPECT_SENTIMENT
FROM STG_FEEDBACK
LIMIT 5;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA1.2 Build the enriched feedback table (score once, query many times)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FEEDBACK_ENRICHED AS
WITH ai_scored AS (
    SELECT f.*, c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.SECTOR AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR, c.RM_NAME,
           -- AI_SENTIMENT returns a label, so map the overall label to -1, 0 or 1
           -- (legacy SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SENTIMENT is blocked on new accounts)
           DECODE(GET(FILTER(AI_SENTIMENT(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT):categories, c -> c:name::STRING = 'overall'), 0):sentiment::STRING,
                  'positive', 1, 'negative', -1, 0)::FLOAT AS SENTIMENT_SCORE,
           AI_CLASSIFY(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT,
               ['Performance Issue','Service Quality','Technical Problem',
                'Positive Experience','Feature Request']) AS CLASSIFICATION_RESULT
    FROM STG_FEEDBACK f
    LEFT JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON f.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
)
SELECT FEEDBACK_ID, FEEDBACK_DATE, CUSTOMER_ID, CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, RM_NAME,
       PAYMENT_ID, FEEDBACK_CHANNEL, FEEDBACK_TEXT, PAYMENT_TYPE, RATING, SENTIMENT_SCORE,
       CASE WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE >  0.3 THEN 'POSITIVE'
            WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE < -0.3 THEN 'NEGATIVE'
            ELSE 'NEUTRAL' END                  AS SENTIMENT_LABEL,
       CLASSIFICATION_RESULT:labels[0]::STRING  AS TOPIC_CATEGORY
FROM ai_scored;

SELECT PAYMENT_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS FEEDBACK,
       ROUND(AVG(SENTIMENT_SCORE), 3) AS AVG_SENTIMENT,
       ROUND(COUNT_IF(SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE') / COUNT(*) * 100, 1) AS NEGATIVE_PCT
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
GROUP BY PAYMENT_TYPE ORDER BY AVG_SENTIMENT;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA1.3 AI_FILTER: natural-language WHERE clause
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, PAYMENT_TYPE, LEFT(FEEDBACK_TEXT, 120) AS FEEDBACK
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
WHERE SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE'
  AND AI_FILTER(PROMPT('Does the client in this feedback explicitly state that they will or may leave the bank, move their business to another bank, review other banking providers, or tender their banking? Complaints without a stated intention to leave do not count. Feedback: {0}', FEEDBACK_TEXT))
LIMIT 10;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA1.4 AI_AGG: themes across many rows, per relationship manager
-- One LLM summary per group - no row limit, no prompt stuffing
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE RM_FEEDBACK_THEMES AS
SELECT RM_NAME,
       COUNT(*) AS NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK,
       AI_AGG(FEEDBACK_TEXT,
              'You are briefing a corporate banking relationship manager. List the top 3 recurring complaint themes in this client feedback, each with a one-line recommended action. Be concise.') AS TOP_THEMES
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
WHERE SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE' AND RM_NAME IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY RM_NAME;

SELECT RM_NAME, NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK, TOP_THEMES FROM RM_FEEDBACK_THEMES ORDER BY NEGATIVE_FEEDBACK DESC;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA1.5 AI_COMPLETE: draft a client-ready response for the worst item
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT CUSTOMER_NAME, FEEDBACK_TEXT,
       AI_COMPLETE('claude-sonnet-4-5',
         'Draft a short, professional reply from a UK corporate bank to this client feedback. Acknowledge the issue, avoid admitting liability, offer a follow-up call. Feedback: ' || FEEDBACK_TEXT) AS DRAFT_REPLY
FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
WHERE SENTIMENT_LABEL = 'NEGATIVE'
ORDER BY SENTIMENT_SCORE
LIMIT 1;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA1.6 Cortex Code prompts
--  "Using FEEDBACK_ENRICHED, show me which customer sectors have worsening
--   sentiment month over month and chart it."
--  "Use AI_EXTRACT on FEEDBACK_TEXT to pull out any payment reference or amount
--   mentioned, into a new table FEEDBACK_ENTITIES."
-- -----------------------------------------------------

SELECT 'DA1 complete' AS STATUS;

modules.title: One trusted answer on client health, for every RM and every agent
modules.prerequisites: DA1 (`FEEDBACK_ENRICHED`), or `setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql`
modules.question: An RM is about to call a corporate client whose payments are failing. The payments report, the RM's spreadsheet and the ops dashboard each give a different success rate. Give the bank one trusted answer that anyone, and any AI agent, can get in plain English.
build: `SV_CLIENT_360`: the bank's single definition of client payments health, alerts and sentiment
The bank's rules and a signed-off answer, so a question RMs actually ask is answered the same way every time
A quality score that proves the answers are right before RMs and agents rely on them

steps.title: The problem this solves
steps.body:
Read this first: it's the story you'll tell the business.
- **Today:** "success rate", "value at risk" and "open incidents" are calculated differently in every report. An RM walks into a client call with one number; the client's ops team has another.
- **The cost:** wasted time reconciling numbers, awkward client conversations, and AI that guesses. Ask a chatbot "which clients are unhappy?" and it writes its own SQL, with its own definitions.
- **The fix:** a semantic view. The bank writes each definition once, in business language, next to the data. People, BI tools, Cortex Analyst and every agent in this lab (OPS1, AI1, AI2, AI3) get the same answer from it.
By the end of this module an RM can ask "Which clients have negative sentiment and a success rate below 96%?" and get the bank's answer, checked, monitored and scored.
What you'll bring together around each client:
| For the RM | Comes from |
|---|---|
| Client, sector and relationship manager | `STG_CUSTOMERS` |
| Payment volume, success rate and value at risk | `V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY` (you build it next) |
| What the client is saying, and how they feel | `FEEDBACK_ENRICHED` (scored in DA1) |
| Open and critical incidents | `V_CLIENT_ALERTS` (you build it next) |
steps.expect: you can explain, in one sentence, why one definition beats three reports.

steps.title: Give the data a stable shape
steps.body: These views are a contract: if the source systems change, you fix one view, and every RM question keeps working.
steps.prompt: In BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS create two views. V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY: one row per CUSTOMER_ID from STG_PAYMENTS joined to STG_ACCOUNTS (on ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID), with TOTAL_PAYMENTS, SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS, FAILED_PAYMENTS, TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP and FAILED_VOLUME_GBP. V_CLIENT_ALERTS: one row per ALERT_ID from BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.OPERATIONAL_ALERTS joined through STG_PAYMENTS and STG_ACCOUNTS to get CUSTOMER_ID, with SEVERITY, ALERT_STATUS, ALERT_TIME and RESOLUTION_TIME_MIN. Show 5 rows from each.
steps.expect: two views, with one row per client in the payment summary.

steps.title: Write the bank's definitions once
steps.body:
1. Click **+ Add new > Semantic view** and name the file `sv_client_360`.
2. Cortex Code opens beside it with its own starter, "Help me create a semantic view", and a **Questions** card. Click **Cancel** on the card.
3. Paste the brief below into the same Cortex Code chat. It names every table and key, so there's nothing left to ask.
4. Press **Allow** on each **Run this command?** card.
**Important:** if Cortex Code still asks about sources, don't pick the RAW_DATA tables or the staging list it suggests. Choose **Other...** and reply "Use exactly the four tables in my brief".
- **Success rate** is defined once: successful over total payments for the client, not an average of averages.
- **Synonyms** mean "RM", "banker" and "relationship manager" all find the same person.
steps.where: banking-hol-pack Workspace > **+ Add new > Semantic view**
steps.prompt: Create a semantic view BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_CLIENT_360 with four logical tables: clients (STG_CUSTOMERS, key CUSTOMER_ID), payments (V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY, key CUSTOMER_ID), feedback (FEEDBACK_ENRICHED, key FEEDBACK_ID) and alerts (V_CLIENT_ALERTS, key ALERT_ID), with payments, feedback and alerts each related to clients on CUSTOMER_ID. Add dimensions including clients.customer_name, clients.sector, clients.rm_name (synonyms "relationship manager", "RM") and feedback.sentiment_label, and metrics including payments.payment_volume (sum of total volume GBP), payments.success_rate_pct, feedback.avg_sentiment, alerts.open_alert_count (status not RESOLVED) and alerts.critical_alert_count. Add business comments and synonyms, then deploy it. Use exactly these four tables and names, and don't ask me which sources to use.
steps.expect: `SV_CLIENT_360` exists. Keep the logical names `clients`, `payments`, `rm_name` and `payment_volume`: the check queries them.
steps.mediaCaption: + Add new > Semantic view > name it sv_client_360, then paste the brief into the Cortex Code panel

steps.title: Answer the RM's question without writing a join
steps.body:
- Analysts get the same numbers as the agents, without rewriting the joins.
- Every KPI's definition is documented and queryable, which model risk and audit teams will ask for.
steps.prompt: Query SV_CLIENT_360 with the SEMANTIC_VIEW function: payment volume, success rate and open alert count by RM name, ordered by open alerts. Then explain which joins the semantic view did for me, and list each metric with the calculation it uses from BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SEMANTIC_METRICS.
steps.expect: one row per RM with volume, success rate and open alerts; an explanation that clients, payments and alerts were joined for you; then each metric with its calculation.

steps.title: Open the definition where the business can refine it
steps.body:
1. If you're on the CoCo side, switch the toggle at the top left to **Home**.
2. Open **AI > Analyst**.
3. In the database picker, choose **BANKING_HOL**, then the **ANALYTICS** schema.
4. Click **SV_CLIENT_360**.
5. In **Open semantic view in Workspaces**, open the **Destination Workspace** dropdown (it says **My Workspace**) and pick **banking-hol-pack**.
6. Click **Open**.
**Tip:** tick **Always open semantic views in this workspace** so you don't have to pick it again.
This is **Semantic Studio**. You change a working copy here; RMs and agents only see a change once you **Deploy** it.
steps.where: Snowsight > **AI > Analyst**, then the banking-hol-pack Workspace
steps.expect: `SV_CLIENT_360.sv.yaml` open in the banking-hol-pack Workspace, under a `cortex_project` folder.
steps.mediaCaption: Home > AI > Analyst > BANKING_HOL > ANALYTICS > SV_CLIENT_360 > Open in banking-hol-pack

steps.title: See what the RM's question relies on
steps.body:
1. On **Visual**, expand **Metrics** under PAYMENTS: these are the bank's KPIs.
2. Click **Diagram**: the client sits in the middle, with payments, feedback and alerts around it.
3. Click **YAML**: the same definition as text, ready for change control in Git.
4. Go back to **Visual** and note the four tabs on the right. You'll use each one next.
| Tab | What it gives the bank |
|---|---|
| **Playground** | try an RM's question before anyone relies on it |
| **Monitoring** | every question RMs and agents ask, and the SQL behind each answer |
| **Suggestions** | KPIs and questions people need that the definition doesn't cover yet |
| **Evaluations** | a quality score, re-run before every change ships |
steps.expect: the Diagram shows CLIENTS in the middle, with ALERTS, FEEDBACK and PAYMENTS joined to it.
steps.mediaCaption: Visual > Diagram > YAML, then the Suggestions, Playground, Monitoring and Evaluations tabs

steps.title: Ask the RM's question
steps.body:
1. Open the **Playground** tab.
2. Type this question in **Enter prompt** and click **Run**: "Which clients have negative sentiment and a success rate below 96%?"
3. Read the SQL in the answer. Look at how it filters on sentiment.
Why it matters:
- An RM never sees this SQL. They'd just hear "no clients at risk" before a difficult call.
- The next two steps fix it the way a bank would: write the rule down, then ask again.
steps.expect: an answer with its SQL. The filter on sentiment may use `'negative'` in lower case, but the data stores labels in upper case (`NEGATIVE`), so it returns no clients. "Negative" could also mean one bad comment or a negative average.
steps.mediaCaption: Playground > type the question > Run, then read the SQL

steps.title: Write down the bank's rules
steps.body:
1. Under **Custom instructions**, hover **SQL generation** and click its edit (pencil) button.
2. Paste the rules below into the box.
3. Click the tick at the top right of the box to save the change to your file.
The bank's definition of an unhappy client now applies to every question and every agent, without retraining anyone.
steps.prompt: Sentiment labels are stored in upper case: POSITIVE, NEUTRAL or NEGATIVE. "Negative sentiment" for a client means their average sentiment score is below 0. Client names are stored in upper case: match them with ILIKE. Round percentages to 1 decimal place.
steps.expect: the rules saved under **SQL generation**.
steps.pasteInto: the **SQL generation** box in Semantic Studio (not the Cortex Code sidebar)
steps.mediaCaption: Custom instructions > SQL generation > edit > paste the rules > save (tick)

steps.title: Ask the RM's question again
steps.body:
1. Type the same question in **Enter prompt** and click **Run**: "Which clients have negative sentiment and a success rate below 96%?"
2. Read the SQL. It should use the average sentiment (or `'NEGATIVE'` in upper case).
steps.expect: a list of at-risk clients, with SQL that follows the bank's rules.

steps.title: Sign off the answer
steps.body:
1. Check the SQL and results of the answer. Only sign it off if it's right.
2. Under the answer, click **Add to verified query**, check the question and SQL, and save it.
**Tip:** you can also add it from **Visual**: click **+** next to **Verified queries**, paste the question, click **Generate SQL**, **Run** it to check the result, then save with the tick.
A signed-off answer is reused whenever anyone asks something similar, so the RM, the ops dashboard and the agent all get the same list of clients.
steps.expect: the question listed under **Verified queries** with a green tick.
steps.mediaCaption: Verified queries > + > paste the question > Generate SQL > Run > save with the tick

steps.title: Make it live for RMs and agents
steps.body:
1. Click **Deploy** in the top bar.
2. In **Deploy changes to...**, tick the **default** target, `BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS`. If it says **Up to date**, you haven't saved a change yet.
3. Click **Deploy**.
From now on, every agent built on `SV_CLIENT_360` (OPS1, AI1) uses the bank's rules and the signed-off answer. In production you'd deploy through Git after review, like any other change.
steps.expect: the deploy succeeds and **Errors (0)** shows at the bottom of the editor.
steps.mediaCaption: Deploy > Deploy changes to... > default BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS > Deploy

steps.title: See what RMs are asking
steps.body:
1. Open the **Monitoring** tab.
2. Click one of your Playground questions.
3. Read the question, the SQL behind the answer and any user feedback.
- This is your early warning: the questions the business really asks, and the answers it got.
- A wrong answer has a **Request ID**: give it to Cortex Code with the right answer and it traces what went wrong.
steps.expect: each question asked, newest first, with the SQL behind it.
steps.mediaCaption: Monitoring > open a question > request ID, status, user feedback and SQL

steps.title: Find what the definition is missing
steps.body:
1. Open the **Suggestions** tab.
2. Expand **Metrics** and read what it proposes.
3. Pick the one an RM would use before a client call, and leave the rest.
**Tip:** add synonyms yourself from the words your RMs really use. Auto-generated synonyms often make answers worse.
steps.expect: suggested KPIs, filters and questions based on the definition and how it's used.

steps.title: Prove it's right before anyone relies on it
steps.body:
1. In the **Playground**, ask two or three similar questions, such as "Which RMs have the most open alerts?" and "Which sectors have the lowest success rate?". Sign off each one under **Verified queries**.
2. Open the **Evaluations** tab and click **Create evaluation run**.
3. Fill it in as below.
4. Click **Run evaluation**. It runs in the background for a few minutes.
| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| **Name** | `da2_baseline` |
| Warehouse | leave as is (`BANKING_WH`) |
| **Metric version** | **v3** (change it from v1: v1 has been retired, so v1 runs fail) |
| **Select verified queries** | **Select all** |
Why it matters:
- The score is evidence for model risk and the business that AI answers are right, not just plausible.
- Re-run it before every change. If a question that used to pass now fails, you catch it before an RM or an agent does.
steps.expect: `da2_baseline` listed under **Evaluations**. Open it when it finishes to see the accuracy score and, for each question, the signed-off SQL next to what Analyst wrote on its own.
steps.mediaCaption: Evaluations > Create evaluation run > name da2_baseline > metric version v3 > select the verified queries > Run evaluation

modules.check: `SV_CLIENT_360` is live with the bank's sentiment rule and a signed-off answer, and "Which clients have negative sentiment and a success rate below 96%?" returns the list of at-risk clients.
modules.note: RMs, ops, BI tools and every AI agent give the same answer on client health, because the bank wrote the definition once. Every question is monitored and every change is scored before it ships, which is what model risk and audit need to approve AI for client-facing work.
modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE DA2: BUILD A SEMANTIC VIEW + ASK CORTEX ANALYST   (~60 min)
-- Persona: Data Analyst
-- Question: "Give RMs and ops a single, trusted definition of a corporate
--            client's payments health that anyone can query in plain English."
-- Prereq:   setup/catchup/core_analytics.sql  (STG_* views, FEEDBACK_ENRICHED)
-- Builds:   V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY, V_CLIENT_ALERTS, SV_CLIENT_360
-- Skipped DA2? setup/catchup/client_360.sql builds the same objects.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BANKING_WH;
USE SCHEMA BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.1 Stable interface views (semantic views should sit on contracts, not raw)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY
    COMMENT = 'One row per corporate client: payment volumes, success and latency'
AS
SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID,
       COUNT(*)                                                     AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
       COUNT_IF(p.IS_SUCCESSFUL)                                    AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
       COUNT_IF(p.IS_FAILED)                                        AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
       SUM(p.AMOUNT)                                                AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
       SUM(IFF(p.IS_FAILED, p.AMOUNT, 0))                           AS FAILED_VOLUME_GBP,
       ROUND(AVG(p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS), 0)                          AS AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
       MAX(p.PAYMENT_DATE)                                          AS LAST_PAYMENT_DATE
FROM STG_PAYMENTS p
JOIN STG_ACCOUNTS  a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW V_CLIENT_ALERTS
    COMMENT = 'Operational alerts attributed to the originating corporate client'
AS
SELECT al.ALERT_ID, a.CUSTOMER_ID, al.ALERT_TIME::TIMESTAMP AS ALERT_TIME,
       al.SEVERITY, al.PAYMENT_TYPE, al.STATUS AS ALERT_STATUS,
       al.ASSIGNED_TO, al.RESOLUTION_TIME_MIN, al.ALERT_DESCRIPTION
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.OPERATIONAL_ALERTS al
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS p ON al.PAYMENT_ID = p.PAYMENT_ID
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.ACCOUNTS a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.2 The semantic view: business names, relationships, metrics, synonyms
-- Tip: you can also build this in Snowsight (AI & ML > Cortex Analyst > Create)
-- or ask CoCo: "Create a semantic view over STG_CUSTOMERS, V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY,
-- FEEDBACK_ENRICHED and V_CLIENT_ALERTS joined on CUSTOMER_ID."
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE SEMANTIC VIEW SV_CLIENT_360

  TABLES (
    clients AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS
      PRIMARY KEY (CUSTOMER_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('customers', 'corporate clients', 'accounts')
      COMMENT = 'Corporate banking clients with KYC status and assigned relationship manager',
    payments AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY
      PRIMARY KEY (CUSTOMER_ID)
      COMMENT = 'Payment activity summary per client',
    feedback AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
      PRIMARY KEY (FEEDBACK_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('complaints', 'customer feedback', 'sentiment')
      COMMENT = 'Client feedback with AI sentiment and topic',
    alerts AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_ALERTS
      PRIMARY KEY (ALERT_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('incidents', 'operational alerts')
      COMMENT = 'Operational payment alerts per client'
  )

  RELATIONSHIPS (
    payments_to_clients AS payments (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES clients,
    feedback_to_clients AS feedback (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES clients,
    alerts_to_clients   AS alerts   (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES clients
  )

  FACTS (
    payments.total_payments      AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
    payments.successful_payments AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
    payments.failed_payments     AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
    payments.total_volume_gbp    AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
    payments.failed_volume_gbp   AS FAILED_VOLUME_GBP,
    feedback.sentiment_score     AS SENTIMENT_SCORE,
    feedback.rating              AS RATING,
    alerts.resolution_time_min   AS RESOLUTION_TIME_MIN
  )

  DIMENSIONS (
    clients.customer_name AS CUSTOMER_NAME
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('client', 'client name', 'company')
      COMMENT = 'Registered legal entity name (upper case)',
    clients.sector        AS SECTOR WITH SYNONYMS = ('industry'),
    clients.country       AS COUNTRY COMMENT = 'ISO alpha-3 country code',
    clients.kyc_status    AS KYC_STATUS COMMENT = 'APPROVED, PENDING_REVIEW, EXPIRED',
    clients.rm_name       AS RM_NAME WITH SYNONYMS = ('relationship manager', 'RM', 'banker'),
    clients.rm_team       AS RM_TEAM COMMENT = 'Corporate, Institutional or SME banking team',
    feedback.sentiment_label AS SENTIMENT_LABEL COMMENT = 'POSITIVE, NEUTRAL, NEGATIVE',
    feedback.topic_category  AS TOPIC_CATEGORY,
    feedback.feedback_payment_type AS PAYMENT_TYPE COMMENT = 'Payment scheme the feedback refers to',
    feedback.feedback_date   AS FEEDBACK_DATE,
    alerts.severity       AS SEVERITY COMMENT = 'LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL',
    alerts.alert_status   AS ALERT_STATUS COMMENT = 'OPEN, ACKNOWLEDGED, INVESTIGATING, RESOLVED',
    alerts.alert_time     AS ALERT_TIME
  )

  METRICS (
    payments.payment_count     AS SUM(payments.total_payments) WITH SYNONYMS = ('number of payments'),
    payments.payment_volume    AS SUM(payments.total_volume_gbp) WITH SYNONYMS = ('volume', 'value'),
    payments.failed_volume     AS SUM(payments.failed_volume_gbp) WITH SYNONYMS = ('value at risk'),
    payments.success_rate_pct  AS ROUND(SUM(payments.successful_payments) / NULLIF(SUM(payments.total_payments), 0) * 100, 2)
      COMMENT = 'Weighted payment success rate %',
    feedback.avg_sentiment     AS ROUND(AVG(feedback.sentiment_score), 3),
    feedback.negative_feedback_count AS COUNT_IF(feedback.sentiment_label = 'NEGATIVE'),
    alerts.open_alert_count    AS COUNT_IF(alerts.alert_status <> 'RESOLVED') WITH SYNONYMS = ('open incidents'),
    alerts.critical_alert_count AS COUNT_IF(alerts.severity = 'CRITICAL'),
    alerts.avg_resolution_min  AS ROUND(AVG(alerts.resolution_time_min), 0)
  )

  COMMENT = 'Corporate Client 360 for Payments Operations: payments health, feedback sentiment and operational alerts per client'

  AI_SQL_GENERATION 'Sentiment labels are stored in upper case: POSITIVE, NEUTRAL or NEGATIVE. "Negative sentiment" for a client means their average sentiment score is below 0. Client names are stored in upper case; match them case-insensitively with ILIKE. Round percentages to 1 decimal place.'

  AI_VERIFIED_QUERIES (
    worst_clients AS (
      QUESTION 'Which 5 clients have the lowest payment success rate?'
      ONBOARDING_QUESTION TRUE
      SQL 'SELECT c.CUSTOMER_NAME, ROUND(SUM(p.SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS) / NULLIF(SUM(p.TOTAL_PAYMENTS), 0) * 100, 2) AS success_rate_pct
           FROM BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY p
           JOIN BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON p.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
           GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_NAME ORDER BY success_rate_pct ASC LIMIT 5'
    ),
    rm_open_alerts AS (
      QUESTION 'How many open alerts does each relationship manager have across their clients?'
      ONBOARDING_QUESTION TRUE
      SQL 'SELECT c.RM_NAME, COUNT_IF(a.ALERT_STATUS <> ''RESOLVED'') AS open_alerts
           FROM BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_ALERTS a
           JOIN BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
           GROUP BY c.RM_NAME ORDER BY open_alerts DESC'
    ),
    negative_sentiment_low_success AS (
      QUESTION 'Which clients have negative sentiment and a success rate below 96%?'
      SQL 'WITH s AS (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, AVG(SENTIMENT_SCORE) AS avg_sentiment
                     FROM BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID)
           SELECT c.CUSTOMER_NAME, ROUND(s.avg_sentiment, 3) AS avg_sentiment,
                  ROUND(p.SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS / NULLIF(p.TOTAL_PAYMENTS, 0) * 100, 1) AS success_rate_pct
           FROM BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY p
           JOIN BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON p.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
           JOIN s ON s.CUSTOMER_ID = p.CUSTOMER_ID
           WHERE s.avg_sentiment < 0 AND p.SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS / NULLIF(p.TOTAL_PAYMENTS, 0) * 100 < 96
           ORDER BY success_rate_pct'
    )
  );

SHOW SEMANTIC METRICS IN SV_CLIENT_360;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.3 Query the semantic view with SQL (no joins to remember)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT * FROM SEMANTIC_VIEW(
    SV_CLIENT_360
    DIMENSIONS clients.rm_name
    METRICS payments.payment_volume, payments.success_rate_pct, alerts.open_alert_count
) ORDER BY open_alert_count DESC;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.4 Semantic Studio (UI): AI > Analyst > SV_CLIENT_360 > open in banking-hol-pack.
-- Visual / YAML / Diagram views; Playground, Monitoring, Suggestions, Evaluations tabs.
-- The AI_SQL_GENERATION rules and the negative_sentiment_low_success verified query above
-- are what attendees add in the Playground steps, then Deploy.
-- Evaluation (UI): Evaluations > Create evaluation run > da2_baseline, metric version v3,
-- select all verified queries. Results also in SQL:
--   SELECT * FROM TABLE(SNOWFLAKE.LOCAL.GET_ANALYST_AI_EVALUATION_DATA(
--     'BANKING_HOL', 'ANALYTICS', 'SV_CLIENT_360', 'SEMANTIC VIEW', 'da2_baseline'));
-- Try:
--   "Which clients have negative sentiment and a success rate below 96%?"
--   "Which clients in Manufacturing have open critical alerts?"
--   "Compare success rate and average sentiment for each RM team"
-- Check the generated SQL each time - that is the point of a trusted semantic layer.
-- -----------------------------------------------------

SELECT 'DA2 complete' AS STATUS;

modules.title: Branch network and catchment analysis
modules.prerequisites: C1 only. Uses the retail branch network in `BANKING_HOL.RETAIL`, built at provisioning
modules.question: Which branches could we consolidate, which nearby branches would absorb their customers, and how much longer would those customers have to travel?
build: Notebook `da3_branch_network` with four maps built from SQL results: the branch network, drive-time catchments, H3 customer density and closure risk
Table `CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH` (every customer's fastest and second-fastest branch by real drive time)
Table `BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT` (saving, footfall, added drive time, lost walk-in access and disruption risk per branch)
Table `BUSINESS_CLOSURE_IMPACT` (the small businesses, charities and clubs that pay cash in at each branch, and how many a closure would leave more than 20 minutes from a counter)
Semantic view `SV_BRANCH_NETWORK` and agent `BRANCH_NETWORK_ADVISOR` that answers consolidation questions in plain English

steps.title: Open the starter notebook and create its service
steps.body:
1. Open `notebooks/` > **da3_branch_network.ipynb** in the file explorer.
- Can't see `notebooks/` and `vignettes/`? You're in the wrong Workspace. Pick **banking-hol-pack** from the Workspace dropdown (top left).
2. In the notebook toolbar, click the arrow next to the status dot (right of the blue run button).
3. Choose **Create new service**.
- Already created one in another module? Pick it under **Select service** instead, usually `USER_SERVICE_1`.
4. Expand **Service settings** in **Connect your notebook** and fill it in as below. Only the three **bold** rows change.
| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Service name | leave the default (e.g. `USER_SERVICE_1`) |
| Artifact repositories | leave as is (`SNOWFLAKE.SNOWPARK.PYPI_SHARED_REPOSITORY`) |
| Enable distributed compute | off |
| Runtime | leave as is (v3.0 · Python 3.12) |
| Compute type | CPU |
| Custom image | leave empty |
| **Compute pool** | **NOTEBOOK_POOL** (change it from HOL_COMPUTE_POOL_CPU) |
| **Idle timeout** | **1 hour** (change it from 24 hours) |
| **External access integrations** | **HOL_NOTEBOOK_ACCESS_INTEGRATION** (lets notebooks reach Postgres and the AI Gateway; set it here so one service works for every notebook module) |
| Secrets | leave empty |
**Trial accounts:** there's no HOL_NOTEBOOK_ACCESS_INTEGRATION (trials don't allow external access). Leave **External access integrations** empty: this module works without it.
5. Click **Create and connect**. The first start takes 1-2 minutes.
6. Check the role is **HOL_PARTICIPANT** and the warehouse is **BANKING_WH** (role and warehouse button in the notebook toolbar).
The starter notebook has one numbered heading per step, so Cortex Code puts each cell in the right place.
A notebook runs on its own **notebook service**, which you create once.
You'll build the analysis as cells in this notebook: Cortex Code adds them, and you run each one.
The data is a synthetic UK retail network in `BANKING_HOL.RETAIL`:
- about 60 branches in 8 cities
- ATMs
- 20,000 retail customers, each with a home location and H3 cell
- a year of branch visits
- the ORS travel times and catchments described above
steps.where: the **banking-hol-pack** Workspace (not My Workspace) > file explorer > `notebooks/da3_branch_network.ipynb`
steps.expect: the starter notebook open in banking-hol-pack with its numbered headings, and the status dot showing the service connected
steps.mediaCaption: Open the notebook > Create new service > NOTEBOOK_POOL, 1 hour, HOL_NOTEBOOK_ACCESS_INTEGRATION

steps.title: Map the branch network
steps.body:
Cortex Code may ask you to allow the run: click **Allow**.
Then turn the result into a map:
1. Under the **network** results, click **Chart**.
2. Set **Chart type** to **Map**.
3. Check **Geo type** is **Lat / Lon**, with **LAT** as latitude and **LON** as longitude.
4. Set **Color by** to **SITE**.
5. Click **Full screen** for a bigger map, then click it again to come back.
Tip: use the mouse wheel to zoom in on a city. The **Full screen** icon is at the bottom right of the map.
steps.where: the Cortex Code sidebar, with `da3_branch_network` open
steps.prompt: In the open notebook da3_branch_network, under heading 1 add a SQL cell named network that returns every branch from BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES plus the standalone ATMs (SITE_TYPE = 'STANDALONE') from BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.ATMS. Columns: SITE ('Branch' or 'ATM'), NAME (the branch name or ATM id), CITY, FORMAT, LAT and LON, with LAT and LON cast to FLOAT. Add no Python cell and no chart code. Run it.
steps.expect: a map of the UK with clusters of branches and ATMs around eight cities, on a real basemap.
steps.mediaCaption: Under the network results > Chart > Chart type: Map > Geo type: Lat / Lon > Color by SITE > Full screen

steps.title: Measure drive-time catchments
steps.body:
Then draw the catchments:
1. Under the **catchments** results, click **Chart**.
2. Set **Chart type** to **Map**.
3. Set **Geo type** to **Geography** and check **Geography column** is **CATCHMENT**.
4. Set **Color by** to a measure, such as **CATCHMENT_KM2** (the catchment's area).
5. Lower **Opacity** so you can see where catchments overlap.
An isochrone follows the road network, so catchments are irregular shapes, not circles.
steps.where: the Cortex Code sidebar, with `da3_branch_network` open
steps.prompt: In the open notebook da3_branch_network, under heading 2 add a SQL cell named catchments that uses BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES (rows with PROFILE 'driving-car' and MINUTES 10) joined to BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES on BRANCH_ID, for the Leeds branches only. Columns: BRANCH_NAME, CATCHMENT (the GEOGRAPHY polygon, unchanged), CATCHMENT_KM2 (ST_AREA divided by 1,000,000, rounded to 1 decimal) and CUSTOMERS_IN_CATCHMENT (the number of Leeds customers in BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS whose HOME_LOCATION is ST_WITHIN the CATCHMENT). Order by CUSTOMERS_IN_CATCHMENT descending. Add no Python cell and no chart code. Run it.
steps.expect: a table of customers inside each Leeds branch's 10 minute drive, and a Leeds map where the city-centre catchments almost completely overlap.
steps.mediaCaption: Under the catchments results > Chart > Chart type: Map > Geo type: Geography > Color by CATCHMENT_KM2

steps.title: Find each customer's fastest branch
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named nearest that creates the table BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH: for every customer in BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS, the fastest and second-fastest branch in the same city by drive time, joining BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL on the customer's HOME_H3_CELL with PROFILE 'driving-car'. Columns: CUSTOMER_ID, CITY, AGE_BAND, SEGMENT, DIGITAL_ACTIVE, NEAREST_BRANCH_ID, NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN, NEAREST_DRIVE_KM, SECOND_BRANCH_ID, SECOND_DRIVE_MIN, and NEAREST_WALK_MIN (the shortest 'foot-walking' time to any branch). Run it and show the median drive and walk minutes per city.
steps.expect: all 20,000 customers, each with two branches. The median drive to a branch is about 7 minutes; walking times are much longer and vary more by city.

steps.title: Find overlapping branches
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named overlaps that finds pairs of branches in the same city whose 10 minute drive catchments in BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES overlap by 80% or more (area of ST_INTERSECTION divided by the smaller catchment), with the straight-line distance between them in km. Run it and explain why these pairs are consolidation candidates.
steps.expect: the Manchester, Glasgow and Leeds city-centre pairs at the top. Their customers can reach either branch in the same drive time.

steps.title: Map customer density with H3
steps.body:
Then draw the cells:
1. Under the **density** results, click **Chart**.
2. Set **Chart type** to **Map**.
3. Set **Geo type** to **H3** and check **H3 column** is **H3_CELL**.
4. Set **Color by** to **CUSTOMERS**.
That's the branch that would be hardest to close.
steps.where: the Cortex Code sidebar, with `da3_branch_network` open
steps.prompt: In the open notebook da3_branch_network, under heading 5 add a SQL cell named density that counts the Cardiff customers in BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS per HOME_H3_CELL (an H3 resolution 8 cell id). Columns: H3_CELL (the HOME_H3_CELL value, unchanged) and CUSTOMERS (the count). Order by CUSTOMERS descending. Add no Python cell and no chart code. Run it.
steps.expect: a heat map of Cardiff with customers clustered around the city, and a separate pocket to the south-west around **Barry**, served by one branch.
steps.mediaCaption: Under the density results > Chart > Chart type: Map > Geo type: H3 > Color by CUSTOMERS

steps.title: Model the closure impact
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named closure_impact that creates the table BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT from CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH, BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES, BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_VISITS and BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL. One row per branch: assume it closes and its customers move to their second-fastest branch. Columns: BRANCH_ID, BRANCH_NAME, CITY, FORMAT, ANNUAL_SAVING_GBP (the branch's ANNUAL_COST_GBP), VISITS_12M, COST_PER_VISIT_GBP, CUSTOMERS_AFFECTED, AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN and P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN (SECOND_DRIVE_MIN minus NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN), LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS (customers within a 15 minute walk of the closing branch but not of the receiving branch, using the 'foot-walking' rows), VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS (not digitally active or aged 75+), MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH (the most common second-fastest branch) and DISRUPTION_RISK (HIGH if P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN is 10 or more or VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS is 200 or more, MEDIUM if P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN is 4 or more or LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS is 100 or more, otherwise LOW). Run it and list the 5 best candidates: LOW risk, highest cost per visit.
steps.expect: Leeds Boar Lane and Manchester King Street at the top: high cost, low footfall, and only a minute or two of extra driving. Barry is HIGH risk: a much longer drive for hundreds of vulnerable customers.

steps.title: Put the closure risk on the map
steps.body:
Then colour the branches by risk:
1. Under the **risk_map** results, click **Chart**.
2. Set **Chart type** to **Map** and check **Geo type** is **Lat / Lon**.
3. Set **Color by** to **DISRUPTION_RISK**.
This is the picture to take to a consolidation review: where the saving is easy and where it isn't.
steps.where: the Cortex Code sidebar, with `da3_branch_network` open
steps.prompt: In the open notebook da3_branch_network, under heading 6 add a SQL cell named risk_map that joins BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT to BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES on BRANCH_ID. Columns: BRANCH_NAME, CITY, DISRUPTION_RISK, ANNUAL_SAVING_GBP, P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN, and LAT and LON cast to FLOAT. Add no Python cell and no chart code. Run it.
steps.expect: 57 branches, with only a handful in green (LOW). London and Manchester are mostly HIGH; **Barry** in south Wales is HIGH too, while Leeds Boar Lane is LOW.
steps.mediaCaption: Under the risk_map results > Chart > Chart type: Map > Color by DISRUPTION_RISK

steps.title: Count the businesses who pay in at each branch
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named business_impact that creates the table BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.BUSINESS_CLOSURE_IMPACT from BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BUSINESS_CUSTOMERS (small businesses, charities and clubs, each with a HOME_BRANCH_ID, HOME_H3_CELL and TREASURER_DIGITAL), BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BUSINESS_CASH_DEPOSITS (CASH_GBP and CHEQUES_GBP paid in at the counter) and the 'driving-car' rows of BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL. One row per home branch: BRANCH_ID, BRANCH_NAME, CITY, BUSINESSES, SMALL_BUSINESSES, CHARITIES, CLUBS, TREASURER_NOT_DIGITAL, CASH_PAID_IN_12M_GBP, AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN (drive to the fastest other branch minus drive to the home branch) and BUSINESSES_OVER_20_MIN (within 20 minutes of their home branch today, over 20 if it closed). Run it and list the 5 branches with the most businesses newly over 20 minutes.
steps.expect: **Barry** far ahead: over 200 businesses, most of them charities and clubs, paying in millions of pounds of cash a year, many with a treasurer who doesn't bank online. Leeds Boar Lane barely appears. The UK's largest high-street banks are designated under the FCA's access to cash rules (PS24/8), which require an assessment of cash deposit needs for business accounts as well as personal ones before a closure.

steps.title: Build the semantic view
steps.body: The location columns are what let the agent answer with a map later.
steps.prompt: Create a semantic view BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_BRANCH_NETWORK over BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT (logical table closures, primary key BRANCH_ID), BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH (logical table customers, primary key CUSTOMER_ID, related to closures on NEAREST_BRANCH_ID), and three location tables so an agent can draw maps: BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES (logical table sites, primary key BRANCH_ID, closures related to it on BRANCH_ID), BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES (logical table catchments, primary key BRANCH_ID, PROFILE, MINUTES, related to closures on BRANCH_ID) and BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS (logical table homes, primary key CUSTOMER_ID, customers related to it on CUSTOMER_ID). Facts for saving, visits, cost per visit, added drive minutes, lost walk-in access and vulnerable customers; dimensions for branch name, city, format, disruption risk, receiving branch, age band, segment and digital active; map dimensions LAT and LON (from sites, cast to FLOAT), PROFILE and MINUTES (from catchments), CATCHMENT_GEOJSON defined as ST_ASGEOJSON(CATCHMENT)::STRING (a GEOGRAPHY column can't be a dimension), and HOME_H3_CELL (from homes, an H3 resolution 8 cell id); metrics total_saving_gbp, branch_count, customer_count and avg_drive_min. Describe the travel times as OpenRouteService drive minutes, and say in the comments which columns draw points, polygons and H3 hexagons. Add a verified query for "Which branches could close with the least added travel time?". Then query it with SEMANTIC_VIEW for total saving and branch count by city and disruption risk, and for customer_count by HOME_H3_CELL in Cardiff.
steps.expect: the semantic view created, a table of savings by city and risk tier, and about 310 Cardiff H3 cells with their customer counts.

steps.title: Ask Cortex Analyst
steps.body:
Ask these in plain English, one at a time:
1. "Which 3 branches in Manchester could close with the least added travel time?"
2. "How much could we save by closing all LOW risk branches with fewer than 500 visits?"
3. "Which branch closure would cost the most customers their walk-in access?"
steps.expect: SQL generated over the semantic view, and answers that match your notebook
steps.mediaCaption: AI > Analyst > BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS > SV_BRANCH_NETWORK opens it in a Workspace

steps.title: Create the branch network advisor agent
steps.prompt: Create a Cortex Agent BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.BRANCH_NETWORK_ADVISOR with display name "Branch Network Advisor" that advises a UK retail bank on its branch network. Tool: a Cortex Analyst tool Analyst on semantic view BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_BRANCH_NETWORK, on warehouse BANKING_WH. Response instructions: for a consolidation question, return a ranked list of candidate branches with annual saving and cost per visit, the branch that absorbs their customers and the added drive time (average and p90 minutes), customers who lose walk-in access, the disruption risk and vulnerable customers affected, and a short 90-day transition plan. Never recommend closing a HIGH disruption-risk branch without saying why and what mitigation is needed. When a question is about where things are, answer with a map: branches as points from LAT and LON (coloured by DISRUPTION_RISK when risk matters), drive-time catchments as polygons from CATCHMENT_GEOJSON, and customer density as H3 hexagons from HOME_H3_CELL coloured by customer count. Sample questions: "What is the consolidation opportunity in Leeds?", "Show the Leeds branches on a map, coloured by disruption risk", "Map the 10 minute drive catchments in Leeds", "Show customer density in Cardiff as an H3 map", "Which branch would be hardest to close, and why?"
steps.expect: Cortex Code drafts the agent, you review it, and it's created. It appears in Snowsight under **AI & ML > Agents**.
steps.mediaCaption: + Add new > Agent > name it branch_network_advisor > Create with CoCo > paste the brief

steps.title: Ask for a consolidation plan
steps.prompt: What is the consolidation opportunity in Leeds? Give me the candidates, the saving, which branch absorbs the customers, the extra drive time, the risk, and a 90-day transition plan.
steps.expect: Leeds Boar Lane recommended, with about GBP 690,000 a year saved, customers moving to Leeds City Centre for a minute or two of extra driving, LOW risk and a phased 90-day plan. Then ask "Should we close Barry?" and see it explain the HIGH risk. Compare the answers with your risk map, then ask the advisor to draw it in the next step.
steps.pasteInto: the **BRANCH_NETWORK_ADVISOR** agent chat (not the Cortex Code sidebar)
steps.mediaCaption: AI > Agent Studio > Branch Network Advisor > Preview, then paste the question

steps.title: See the network on a map
steps.body:
Then ask, one at a time:
1. "Map the 10 minute drive catchments in Leeds."
2. "Show customer density in Cardiff as an H3 map."

modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE DA3: BRANCH NETWORK AND CATCHMENT ANALYSIS   (~45 min)
-- Persona:  Data Analyst (Retail Banking)
-- Question: "Which branches could we consolidate, who absorbs their
--            customers, and how much longer would those customers travel?"
-- Prereq:   C1 only. Uses BANKING_HOL.RETAIL (setup/07_retail_geo_seed.sql),
--           including real road-network travel times and catchments that were
--           precomputed with OpenRouteService on Snowpark Container Services.
-- In the lab you build this in a Workspace Notebook (da3_branch_network)
-- with Cortex Code; this file is the reference SQL for each cell.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE WAREHOUSE BANKING_WH;
USE SCHEMA BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.1 Map the network (notebook: SQL cell, then Chart > Map > Lat / Lon)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT 'Branch' AS SITE, BRANCH_NAME AS NAME, CITY, FORMAT, LAT::FLOAT AS LAT, LON::FLOAT AS LON
FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES
UNION ALL
SELECT 'ATM', ATM_ID, NULL, NULL, LAT::FLOAT, LON::FLOAT
FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.ATMS WHERE SITE_TYPE = 'STANDALONE';

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.2 Leeds drive-time catchments (notebook: SQL cell, then Chart > Map >
-- Geography). ORS isochrones + ST_WITHIN
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT b.BRANCH_NAME, i.CATCHMENT,
       ROUND(ST_AREA(i.CATCHMENT) / 1e6, 1) AS CATCHMENT_KM2,
       COUNT(c.CUSTOMER_ID) AS CUSTOMERS_IN_CATCHMENT
FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES i
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b USING (BRANCH_ID)
LEFT JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c
  ON c.CITY = 'Leeds' AND ST_WITHIN(c.HOME_LOCATION, i.CATCHMENT)
WHERE i.PROFILE = 'driving-car' AND i.MINUTES = 10 AND b.CITY = 'Leeds'
GROUP BY b.BRANCH_NAME, i.CATCHMENT
ORDER BY CUSTOMERS_IN_CATCHMENT DESC;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.3 Nearest branch by real drive time: each customer's fastest and
-- second-fastest branch from the ORS matrix (by the customer's H3 cell)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH AS
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, t.BRANCH_ID, t.DURATION_S / 60 AS DRIVE_MIN, t.DISTANCE_M / 1000 AS DRIVE_KM,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.CUSTOMER_ID ORDER BY t.DURATION_S) AS RN
    FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c
    JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL t
      ON t.H3_CELL = c.HOME_H3_CELL AND t.PROFILE = 'driving-car'
    JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b ON b.BRANCH_ID = t.BRANCH_ID AND b.CITY = c.CITY
    QUALIFY RN <= 2
),
walk AS (
    SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, MIN(t.DURATION_S) / 60 AS NEAREST_WALK_MIN
    FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c
    JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL t ON t.H3_CELL = c.HOME_H3_CELL AND t.PROFILE = 'foot-walking'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.CITY, c.AGE_BAND, c.SEGMENT, c.DIGITAL_ACTIVE,
       MAX(IFF(r.RN = 1, r.BRANCH_ID, NULL))          AS NEAREST_BRANCH_ID,
       ROUND(MAX(IFF(r.RN = 1, r.DRIVE_MIN, NULL)), 1) AS NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN,
       ROUND(MAX(IFF(r.RN = 1, r.DRIVE_KM, NULL)), 2)  AS NEAREST_DRIVE_KM,
       MAX(IFF(r.RN = 2, r.BRANCH_ID, NULL))          AS SECOND_BRANCH_ID,
       ROUND(MAX(IFF(r.RN = 2, r.DRIVE_MIN, NULL)), 1) AS SECOND_DRIVE_MIN,
       ROUND(ANY_VALUE(w.NEAREST_WALK_MIN), 1)        AS NEAREST_WALK_MIN
FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c
JOIN ranked r USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
LEFT JOIN walk w USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.CITY, c.AGE_BAND, c.SEGMENT, c.DIGITAL_ACTIVE;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.4 Overlapping catchments: branch pairs whose 10 minute drive
-- catchments overlap most (ST_INTERSECTION of the isochrones)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT * FROM (
SELECT a.CITY, a.BRANCH_NAME AS BRANCH_A, b.BRANCH_NAME AS BRANCH_B,
       ROUND(ST_DISTANCE(a.LOCATION, b.LOCATION) / 1000, 2) AS STRAIGHT_LINE_KM,
       ROUND(ST_AREA(ST_INTERSECTION(ia.CATCHMENT, ib.CATCHMENT)) / LEAST(ST_AREA(ia.CATCHMENT), ST_AREA(ib.CATCHMENT)) * 100) AS OVERLAP_PCT
FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES a
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b ON a.CITY = b.CITY AND a.BRANCH_ID < b.BRANCH_ID
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES ia ON ia.BRANCH_ID = a.BRANCH_ID AND ia.PROFILE = 'driving-car' AND ia.MINUTES = 10
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES ib ON ib.BRANCH_ID = b.BRANCH_ID AND ib.PROFILE = 'driving-car' AND ib.MINUTES = 10
) WHERE OVERLAP_PCT >= 80
ORDER BY OVERLAP_PCT DESC, STRAIGHT_LINE_KM;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.5 Customer density with H3 (notebook: SQL cell, then Chart > Map > H3).
-- Resolution 8, ~0.7 km2 cells
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT HOME_H3_CELL AS H3_CELL, COUNT(*) AS CUSTOMERS
FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS
WHERE CITY = 'Cardiff'
GROUP BY HOME_H3_CELL
ORDER BY CUSTOMERS DESC;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.6 Closure impact: if a branch closes, its customers move to their
-- second-fastest branch. Added drive time, lost walk-in access, cost saved.
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT AS
WITH visits AS (
    SELECT BRANCH_ID, COUNT(*) AS VISITS_12M FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_VISITS GROUP BY 1
),
walk_after AS (
    -- walking time to the receiving branch for each customer
    SELECT n.CUSTOMER_ID, t.DURATION_S / 60 AS WALK_MIN_AFTER
    FROM CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH n
    JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS c USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
    JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL t
      ON t.H3_CELL = c.HOME_H3_CELL AND t.BRANCH_ID = n.SECOND_BRANCH_ID AND t.PROFILE = 'foot-walking'
),
moved AS (
    SELECT n.NEAREST_BRANCH_ID AS BRANCH_ID,
           COUNT(*) AS CUSTOMERS,
           ROUND(AVG(n.SECOND_DRIVE_MIN - n.NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN), 1) AS AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
           ROUND(APPROX_PERCENTILE(n.SECOND_DRIVE_MIN - n.NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN, 0.9), 1) AS P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
           COUNT_IF(n.NEAREST_WALK_MIN <= 15 AND COALESCE(w.WALK_MIN_AFTER, 999) > 15) AS LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS,
           COUNT_IF(NOT n.DIGITAL_ACTIVE OR n.AGE_BAND = '75+') AS VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS,
           MODE(n.SECOND_BRANCH_ID) AS MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH_ID
    FROM CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH n
    LEFT JOIN walk_after w USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT b.BRANCH_ID, b.BRANCH_NAME, b.CITY, b.FORMAT, b.ANNUAL_COST_GBP AS ANNUAL_SAVING_GBP,
       COALESCE(v.VISITS_12M, 0) AS VISITS_12M,
       ROUND(b.ANNUAL_COST_GBP / NULLIF(v.VISITS_12M, 0), 2) AS COST_PER_VISIT_GBP,
       m.CUSTOMERS AS CUSTOMERS_AFFECTED, m.AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN, m.P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
       m.LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS, m.VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS, r.BRANCH_NAME AS MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH,
       CASE WHEN m.P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN >= 10 OR m.VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS >= 200 THEN 'HIGH'
            WHEN m.P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN >= 4 OR m.LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS >= 100 THEN 'MEDIUM' ELSE 'LOW' END AS DISRUPTION_RISK
FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b
JOIN moved m ON m.BRANCH_ID = b.BRANCH_ID
LEFT JOIN visits v ON v.BRANCH_ID = b.BRANCH_ID
LEFT JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES r ON r.BRANCH_ID = m.MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH_ID;

SELECT BRANCH_NAME, CITY, ANNUAL_SAVING_GBP, COST_PER_VISIT_GBP, AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN, P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
       LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS, VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS, DISRUPTION_RISK, MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH
FROM BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT
ORDER BY DISRUPTION_RISK = 'LOW' DESC, COST_PER_VISIT_GBP DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.6a Risk on the map (notebook: SQL cell, then Chart > Map > Lat / Lon,
-- coloured by DISRUPTION_RISK)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT c.BRANCH_NAME, c.CITY, c.DISRUPTION_RISK, c.ANNUAL_SAVING_GBP, c.P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
       b.LAT::FLOAT AS LAT, b.LON::FLOAT AS LON
FROM BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT c
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b USING (BRANCH_ID);

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.6b Who else pays in here: small businesses, charities and clubs
-- that deposit cash at the counter. Same move-to-second-fastest rule.
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE BUSINESS_CLOSURE_IMPACT AS
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT b.BUSINESS_ID, b.BUSINESS_TYPE, b.HOME_BRANCH_ID, b.TREASURER_DIGITAL, t.BRANCH_ID, t.DURATION_S / 60 AS DRIVE_MIN,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY b.BUSINESS_ID ORDER BY t.DURATION_S) AS RN
    FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BUSINESS_CUSTOMERS b
    JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL t ON t.H3_CELL = b.HOME_H3_CELL AND t.PROFILE = 'driving-car'
),
per_business AS (
    SELECT BUSINESS_ID, ANY_VALUE(BUSINESS_TYPE) AS BUSINESS_TYPE, ANY_VALUE(TREASURER_DIGITAL) AS TREASURER_DIGITAL,
           ANY_VALUE(HOME_BRANCH_ID) AS BRANCH_ID,
           MAX(IFF(BRANCH_ID = HOME_BRANCH_ID, DRIVE_MIN, NULL)) AS HOME_DRIVE_MIN,
           MIN(IFF(BRANCH_ID <> HOME_BRANCH_ID, DRIVE_MIN, NULL)) AS NEXT_DRIVE_MIN
    FROM ranked GROUP BY 1
),
cash AS (SELECT BUSINESS_ID, SUM(CASH_GBP + CHEQUES_GBP) AS PAID_IN_GBP FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BUSINESS_CASH_DEPOSITS GROUP BY 1)
SELECT p.BRANCH_ID, br.BRANCH_NAME, br.CITY,
       COUNT(*) AS BUSINESSES,
       COUNT_IF(p.BUSINESS_TYPE = 'SMALL_BUSINESS') AS SMALL_BUSINESSES,
       COUNT_IF(p.BUSINESS_TYPE = 'CHARITY') AS CHARITIES,
       COUNT_IF(p.BUSINESS_TYPE = 'CLUB') AS CLUBS,
       COUNT_IF(NOT p.TREASURER_DIGITAL) AS TREASURER_NOT_DIGITAL,
       ROUND(SUM(c.PAID_IN_GBP)) AS CASH_PAID_IN_12M_GBP,
       ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(p.NEXT_DRIVE_MIN, 60) - p.HOME_DRIVE_MIN), 1) AS AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN,
       COUNT_IF(p.HOME_DRIVE_MIN <= 20 AND COALESCE(p.NEXT_DRIVE_MIN, 999) > 20) AS BUSINESSES_OVER_20_MIN
FROM per_business p
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES br ON br.BRANCH_ID = p.BRANCH_ID
LEFT JOIN cash c USING (BUSINESS_ID)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3;

SELECT BRANCH_NAME, CITY, BUSINESSES, CHARITIES, CLUBS, TREASURER_NOT_DIGITAL, CASH_PAID_IN_12M_GBP, BUSINESSES_OVER_20_MIN
FROM BUSINESS_CLOSURE_IMPACT
ORDER BY BUSINESSES_OVER_20_MIN DESC LIMIT 5;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.7 Semantic view for Cortex Analyst, with map-ready location columns:
-- branch LAT/LON points, home H3 cells and catchment polygons as GeoJSON text
-- (a GEOGRAPHY column can't be a dimension: it can't be grouped by)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE SEMANTIC VIEW SV_BRANCH_NETWORK
  TABLES (
    closures AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.BRANCH_CLOSURE_IMPACT
      PRIMARY KEY (BRANCH_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('branches', 'branch closures', 'consolidation candidates')
      COMMENT = 'One row per branch: what happens if it closes',
    sites AS BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES
      PRIMARY KEY (BRANCH_ID)
      COMMENT = 'Branch locations',
    catchments AS BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_ISOCHRONES
      PRIMARY KEY (BRANCH_ID, PROFILE, MINUTES)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('isochrones', 'drive-time catchments')
      COMMENT = 'Area reachable from each branch within a 10 or 20 minute drive or a 15 minute walk (OpenRouteService)',
    customers AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.CUSTOMER_NEAREST_BRANCH
      PRIMARY KEY (CUSTOMER_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('retail customers', 'catchment')
      COMMENT = 'Each retail customer with their fastest and second-fastest branch by drive time',
    homes AS BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.RETAIL_CUSTOMERS
      PRIMARY KEY (CUSTOMER_ID)
      COMMENT = 'Customer home locations'
  )
  RELATIONSHIPS (
    closures (BRANCH_ID) REFERENCES sites,
    catchments (BRANCH_ID) REFERENCES closures,
    customers (NEAREST_BRANCH_ID) REFERENCES closures,
    customers (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES homes
  )
  FACTS (
    closures.annual_saving_gbp AS ANNUAL_SAVING_GBP COMMENT = 'Annual running cost saved if the branch closes (GBP)',
    closures.visits_12m AS VISITS_12M COMMENT = 'Branch visits in the last 12 months',
    closures.cost_per_visit_gbp AS COST_PER_VISIT_GBP COMMENT = 'Annual cost divided by visits',
    closures.avg_added_drive_min AS AVG_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN WITH SYNONYMS = ('extra travel time') COMMENT = 'Average extra drive minutes to the next-fastest branch (OpenRouteService)',
    closures.p90_added_drive_min AS P90_ADDED_DRIVE_MIN COMMENT = '90th percentile extra drive minutes',
    closures.lose_walk_in_access AS LOSE_WALK_IN_ACCESS COMMENT = 'Customers who lose a branch within a 15 minute walk',
    closures.vulnerable_customers AS VULNERABLE_CUSTOMERS COMMENT = 'Affected customers who are 75+ or not digitally active',
    customers.nearest_drive_min AS NEAREST_DRIVE_MIN COMMENT = 'Drive minutes from home to the fastest branch',
    customers.nearest_walk_min AS NEAREST_WALK_MIN COMMENT = 'Walking minutes from home to the nearest branch'
  )
  DIMENSIONS (
    closures.branch_name AS BRANCH_NAME WITH SYNONYMS = ('branch') COMMENT = 'Branch name',
    closures.city AS CITY COMMENT = 'City',
    closures.format AS FORMAT COMMENT = 'FULL or EXPRESS branch',
    closures.disruption_risk AS DISRUPTION_RISK COMMENT = 'LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH service disruption if closed',
    closures.main_receiving_branch AS MAIN_RECEIVING_BRANCH COMMENT = 'Branch that absorbs most customers',
    sites.lat AS LAT::FLOAT COMMENT = 'Branch latitude: plot branches on a map with LAT and LON',
    sites.lon AS LON::FLOAT COMMENT = 'Branch longitude',
    catchments.profile AS PROFILE COMMENT = 'Travel mode: driving-car or foot-walking',
    catchments.minutes AS MINUTES COMMENT = 'Catchment size in minutes: 10 or 20 (driving-car), 15 (foot-walking)',
    catchments.catchment_geojson AS ST_ASGEOJSON(CATCHMENT)::STRING WITH SYNONYMS = ('catchment polygon', 'isochrone') COMMENT = 'Catchment polygon as GeoJSON: draw it on a map as a polygon',
    customers.age_band AS AGE_BAND COMMENT = 'Customer age band',
    customers.segment AS SEGMENT COMMENT = 'MASS, AFFLUENT or SMALL_BUSINESS',
    customers.digital_active AS DIGITAL_ACTIVE COMMENT = 'Customer uses digital banking',
    homes.home_h3_cell AS HOME_H3_CELL WITH SYNONYMS = ('hexagon', 'H3 cell') COMMENT = 'H3 resolution 8 cell (about 0.7 km2) of the customer home: count customers per cell for a density map'
  )
  METRICS (
    closures.total_saving_gbp AS SUM(closures.annual_saving_gbp) COMMENT = 'Total annual saving (GBP)',
    closures.branch_count AS COUNT(closures.branch_name) COMMENT = 'Number of branches',
    customers.customer_count AS COUNT(customers.customer_id) COMMENT = 'Number of customers',
    customers.avg_drive_min AS ROUND(AVG(customers.nearest_drive_min), 1) COMMENT = 'Average drive minutes to the fastest branch'
  )
  COMMENT = 'DA3 retail branch network and consolidation impact (OpenRouteService travel times), with map-ready locations'
;

SELECT * FROM SEMANTIC_VIEW(SV_BRANCH_NETWORK
  METRICS closures.total_saving_gbp, closures.branch_count
  DIMENSIONS closures.city, closures.disruption_risk)
ORDER BY CITY, DISRUPTION_RISK;

-- map-ready: customers per H3 cell in Cardiff, and the Leeds 10 minute catchments
SELECT * FROM SEMANTIC_VIEW(SV_BRANCH_NETWORK
  METRICS customers.customer_count DIMENSIONS homes.home_h3_cell, closures.city)
WHERE CITY = 'Cardiff' ORDER BY CUSTOMER_COUNT DESC LIMIT 5;
SELECT BRANCH_NAME, LEFT(CATCHMENT_GEOJSON, 60) AS POLYGON FROM SEMANTIC_VIEW(SV_BRANCH_NETWORK
  DIMENSIONS closures.branch_name, closures.city, catchments.profile, catchments.minutes, catchments.catchment_geojson)
WHERE CITY = 'Leeds' AND PROFILE = 'driving-car' AND MINUTES = 10;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA3.8 Branch network agent (in the lab: + > Agent > Create with CoCo)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CREATE OR REPLACE AGENT BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.BRANCH_NETWORK_ADVISOR
  COMMENT = 'DA3: retail branch consolidation advisor'
  PROFILE = '{"display_name": "Branch Network Advisor", "color": "orange"}'
  FROM SPECIFICATION
  $$
  models:
    orchestration: auto
  instructions:
    response: >
      You advise a UK retail bank on its branch network. For a consolidation question, return:
      a ranked list of candidate branches with annual saving and cost per visit, the branch that
      absorbs their customers and the added drive time (average and p90 minutes), customers who
      lose walk-in access, the disruption risk and vulnerable customers affected, and a short
      90-day transition plan. Never recommend closing a HIGH disruption-risk branch without
      saying why and what mitigation is needed.
      When a question is about where things are, answer with a map: branches as points from LAT
      and LON (coloured by DISRUPTION_RISK when risk matters), drive-time catchments as polygons
      from CATCHMENT_GEOJSON, and customer density as H3 hexagons from HOME_H3_CELL coloured by
      customer count.
    orchestration: "Use the Analyst tool for every question about branches, closures, catchments, travel time, customers and locations."
    sample_questions:
      - question: "What is the consolidation opportunity in Leeds?"
      - question: "Show the Leeds branches on a map, coloured by disruption risk"
      - question: "Map the 10 minute drive catchments in Leeds"
      - question: "Show customer density in Cardiff as an H3 map"
      - question: "Which branch would be hardest to close, and why?"
  tools:
    - tool_spec:
        type: "cortex_analyst_text_to_sql"
        name: "Analyst"
        description: "Retail branch network: closure impact per branch (saving, visits, added drive time, lost walk-in access, disruption risk), customer catchments, and map-ready locations (branch LAT/LON, catchment polygons as GeoJSON, customer home H3 cells)."
  tool_resources:
    Analyst:
      semantic_view: "BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.SV_BRANCH_NETWORK"
      execution_environment:
        type: "warehouse"
        warehouse: "BANKING_WH"
  $$;

SELECT 'DA3 complete' AS STATUS;

modules.title: Drive-time matrices with OpenRouteService

modules.question: How do we answer "how far is each neighbourhood from a branch, and from the next one if it closes?" for every neighbourhood at once, from real roads, without customer locations leaving the bank?

steps.sql:
SELECT b.BRANCH_NAME, ROUND(t.DURATION_S / 60, 1) AS DRIVE_MIN, ROUND(t.DISTANCE_M / 1000, 1) AS ROAD_KM,
       ROUND(ST_DISTANCE(b.LOCATION, H3_CELL_TO_POINT(t.H3_CELL)) / 1000, 1) AS STRAIGHT_LINE_KM,
       ST_Y(b.LOCATION)::FLOAT AS LAT, ST_X(b.LOCATION)::FLOAT AS LON
FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL t JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b USING (BRANCH_ID)
WHERE t.PROFILE = 'driving-car' AND t.H3_CELL = H3_LATLNG_TO_CELL_STRING(53.4794, -2.2453, 8)
ORDER BY DRIVE_MIN;
steps.expect: road distances well above the straight line. Altrincham is about 12 km away as the crow flies but nearly 20 km by road.

steps.title: Build the closure lookup
steps.body:
This is the question the executive demo answers when you click a hexagon: how far is the nearest branch, and how far is the next one if it closes?
1. Rank every branch for every cell, and keep the first two:
steps.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE MY_CLOSURE_LOOKUP AS
WITH d AS (SELECT t.H3_CELL, t.BRANCH_ID, b.CITY, t.DURATION_S / 60 AS MINS,
                  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.H3_CELL ORDER BY t.DURATION_S) AS RANK

FROM BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCH_CELL_TRAVEL t JOIN BANKING_HOL.RETAIL.BRANCHES b USING (BRANCH_ID)
WHERE t.PROFILE = 'driving-car' AND t.H3_CELL = H3_LATLNG_TO_CELL_STRING(53.4794, -2.2453, 8)

-- 3.
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE MY_CLOSURE_LOOKUP AS
WITH d AS (SELECT t.H3_CELL, t.BRANCH_ID, b.CITY, t.DURATION_S / 60 AS MINS,
                  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY t.H3_CELL ORDER BY t.DURATION_S) AS RANK

       MAX(IFF(RANK = 1, BRANCH_ID, NULL)) AS NEAREST_BRANCH,
       MAX(IFF(RANK = 1, MINS, NULL)) AS NEAREST_MIN,
       MAX(IFF(RANK = 2, BRANCH_ID, NULL)) AS NEXT_BRANCH,

SELECT l.NEAREST_BRANCH, b.BRANCH_NAME, COUNT(c.CUSTOMER_ID) AS CUSTOMERS,
       COUNT_IF(c.CUSTOMER_ID IS NOT NULL AND l.NEAREST_MIN <= 20 AND COALESCE(l.NEXT_MIN, 999) > 20) AS CUSTOMERS_CUT_OFF,

modules.title: Customer lifetime value, value at risk and next-best offers
modules.persona: Data Analyst (Retail Banking, customer value management)
modules.prerequisites: DS4, which builds `ML.RB_CUSTOMER_PREDICTIONS`. If you skipped it, run `setup/catchup/ds1_model.sql` then `setup/catchup/ds4_predictions.sql` first
modules.question: Of the customers who might leave, which ones are worth the most to keep, how much value is at stake, and what should we offer each of them?
build: Table `ANALYTICS.CUSTOMER_VALUE`: every customer's 5-year lifetime value and value at risk
Table `ANALYTICS.CUSTOMER_VALUE_SEGMENTS`: four value-and-risk segments and a rules-based next-best offer per customer
A save list ranked by value at risk, and a chart of where the value is

steps.title: Look at what the models give you
steps.body: 1. Paste and run:
steps.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS CUSTOMERS,
       ROUND(AVG(CHURN_3M) * 100, 2) AS AVG_CHANCE_OF_LEAVING_PCT,
       ROUND(AVG(PREDICTED_MONTHLY_MARGIN_GBP), 2) AS AVG_MONTHLY_MARGIN_GBP,
       ANY_VALUE(ATTRITION_MODEL_VERSION) AS ATTRITION_MODEL, ANY_VALUE(MARGIN_MODEL_VERSION) AS MARGIN_MODEL
FROM BANKING_HOL.ML.RB_CUSTOMER_PREDICTIONS;
steps.expect: about 18,400 customers, a 2% average chance of leaving in 3 months, about £20 of margin a month, and the model versions that produced them

steps.title: Lifetime value and value at risk
steps.body: 1. Paste and run:
steps.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE CUSTOMER_VALUE AS
WITH k AS (
    -- nobody is certain to stay: floor the 3-month chance of leaving at 0.1%
    SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, GREATEST(CHURN_3M, 0.001) AS CHURN_3M, PREDICTED_MONTHLY_MARGIN_GBP AS MARGIN,
           POWER(1 - GREATEST(CHURN_3M, 0.001), 1 / 3) AS RETENTION,  -- chance of staying each month
           POWER(1.10, 1 / 12) - 1 AS DISCOUNT               -- 10% a year, monthly
    FROM BANKING_HOL.ML.RB_CUSTOMER_PREDICTIONS),
q AS (SELECT *, RETENTION / (1 + DISCOUNT) AS Q FROM k)
SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, CHURN_3M, ROUND(MARGIN, 2) AS MONTHLY_MARGIN_GBP,
       ROUND(1 / (1 - RETENTION) / 12, 1) AS EXPECTED_YEARS,
       -- 60 months of margin, each weighted by the chance they're still here and discounted
       ROUND(MARGIN * Q * (1 - POWER(Q, 60)) / (1 - Q)) AS LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP,
       -- what we expect to lose in the next 12 months: the value of customers worth keeping, times the chance they go
       ROUND(GREATEST(MARGIN * Q * (1 - POWER(Q, 60)) / (1 - Q), 0) * (1 - POWER(RETENTION, 12))) AS VALUE_AT_RISK_GBP
FROM q;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS CUSTOMERS, ROUND(MEDIAN(LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP)) AS MEDIAN_LTV, ROUND(AVG(LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP)) AS AVG_LTV,
       ROUND(SUM(LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP)) AS TOTAL_LTV, ROUND(SUM(VALUE_AT_RISK_GBP)) AS VALUE_AT_RISK
FROM CUSTOMER_VALUE;
steps.expect: a skewed picture. The median customer is worth a little over £100 over 5 years, the average several times that, and some are loss-making (a negative lifetime value). Value at risk counts only the customers worth keeping.

steps.title: Segments and next-best offers
steps.body:
High value is the top quarter by lifetime value; high risk is the fifth most likely to leave.
| | Low risk | High risk |
|---|---|---|
| **High value** | **Grow**: offer the next product | **Save now**: a named adviser calls |
| **Low value** | **Maintain** | **Serve digitally**: lower-cost channels |
The offer is a set of rules in priority order, using the signals DS1 found: a legacy saver gets a better rate, a falling salary gets support, a closing branch gets an introduction to digital and the next branch.
1. Paste and run:
steps.sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE CUSTOMER_VALUE_SEGMENTS AS
WITH v AS (
    SELECT v.*, f.PRODUCTS_HELD, f.ON_LEGACY_SAVER, f.SALARY_TREND, f.DIGITAL_ACTIVE, f.BRANCH_AT_RISK, f.SAVINGS_BALANCE,
           v.LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP >= PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY v.LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP) OVER () AS HIGH_VALUE,
           v.CHURN_3M >= PERCENTILE_CONT(0.80) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY v.CHURN_3M) OVER () AS HIGH_RISK
    FROM CUSTOMER_VALUE v JOIN BANKING_HOL.ML.RB_CHURN_FEATURES f USING (CUSTOMER_ID))
SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP, VALUE_AT_RISK_GBP, CHURN_3M,
       CASE WHEN HIGH_VALUE AND HIGH_RISK THEN 'Save now'
            WHEN HIGH_VALUE THEN 'Grow'
            WHEN HIGH_RISK THEN 'Serve digitally'
            ELSE 'Maintain' END AS SEGMENT,
       CASE WHEN ON_LEGACY_SAVER = 1 THEN 'Move to a better savings rate'
            WHEN SALARY_TREND < 0.8 THEN 'Payment holiday or budgeting support'
            WHEN BRANCH_AT_RISK = 1 THEN 'Branch change: introduce digital and nearest branch'
            WHEN NOT DIGITAL_ACTIVE AND HIGH_RISK THEN 'App onboarding call'
            WHEN HIGH_VALUE AND HIGH_RISK THEN 'Retention call from a named adviser'
            WHEN HIGH_VALUE AND PRODUCTS_HELD <= 2 THEN 'Cross-sell: ISA or credit card'
            WHEN HIGH_VALUE AND SAVINGS_BALANCE >= 20000 THEN 'Premier upgrade'
            WHEN HIGH_VALUE THEN 'Thank-you: fee-free month'
            ELSE 'No action' END AS NEXT_BEST_OFFER
FROM v;
SELECT SEGMENT, COUNT(*) AS CUSTOMERS, ROUND(SUM(LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP)) AS LIFETIME_VALUE, ROUND(SUM(VALUE_AT_RISK_GBP)) AS VALUE_AT_RISK
FROM CUSTOMER_VALUE_SEGMENTS GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY VALUE_AT_RISK DESC;
steps.expect: **Save now** is a few percent of customers but holds about a third of the value at risk. That's the list to work first.

2. Ask Cortex Code for the picture:

modules.note: - **Agree the definition with finance.** Use the same customer profitability numbers finance reports, and agree the horizon and discount rate, so CVM and finance mean the same thing by "worth". - **Rules first, then models.** A transparent offer policy is easy to approve and audit. Once campaigns record who took which offer, the data scientists can train a propensity model per offer and measure uplift. - **Consumer Duty.** Value-based treatment must still give every customer fair value: check what the "Serve digitally" and "Maintain" segments are offered, and how vulnerable customers are treated. - **Put it where people ask.** Add lifetime value and value at risk to a semantic view (DA2) so relationship managers can ask "who in my book is most at risk?" in plain English. DA6 does this with level of detail metrics, comparing every branch and neighbourhood with its city and the UK.

    FROM BANKING_HOL.ML.RB_CUSTOMER_PREDICTIONS),
q AS (SELECT *, RETENTION / (1 + DISCOUNT) AS Q FROM k)

       ROUND(1 / (1 - RETENTION) / 12, 1) AS EXPECTED_YEARS,
       -- 60 months of margin, each weighted by the chance they're still here and discounted

       ROUND(GREATEST(MARGIN * Q * (1 - POWER(Q, 60)) / (1 - Q), 0) * (1 - POWER(RETENTION, 12))) AS VALUE_AT_RISK_GBP
FROM q;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS CUSTOMERS, ROUND(MEDIAN(LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP)) AS MEDIAN_LTV, ROUND(AVG(LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP)) AS AVG_LTV,
       ROUND(SUM(LIFETIME_VALUE_GBP)) AS TOTAL_LTV, ROUND(SUM(VALUE_AT_RISK_GBP)) AS VALUE_AT_RISK
FROM CUSTOMER_VALUE;

-- 4.
