modules.check: Downstream lineage from `RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS` reaches `PAYMENTS_AUDIT_AGENT`, the agent's questions show in query history, and `PAYMENT_SLA_DAILY` is documented.
modules.note: ACCOUNT_USAGE views have up to ~3 hours latency - run history queries at the end of the session.
modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- VIGNETTE GOV2: LINEAGE, AUDIT AND TRUST   (~30 min)
-- Persona: Governance / Risk / Audit
-- Question: "If a source Iceberg table changes, what breaks? And who - human
--            or AI agent - has been reading client data?"
-- Prereq:   C1 only. Uses the ready-made audit pack in BANKING_HOL.AUDIT_PACK
--           (setup/06_audit_pack.sql); ask PAYMENTS_AUDIT_AGENT a few questions first.
-- Note:     ACCOUNT_USAGE views have up to ~3 hours latency. Run the
--           immediate checks first; revisit the history queries at the end of the day.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BANKING_WH;
USE SCHEMA BANKING_HOL.AUDIT_PACK;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- GOV2.1 Impact analysis: what depends on the PAYMENTS Iceberg table? (immediate)
-- Snowsight: Catalog > BANKING_HOL > RAW_DATA > PAYMENTS > Lineage tab
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT DISTANCE, TARGET_OBJECT_DOMAIN, TARGET_OBJECT_DATABASE || '.' || TARGET_OBJECT_SCHEMA || '.' || TARGET_OBJECT_NAME AS DOWNSTREAM_OBJECT
FROM TABLE(SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE('BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS', 'TABLE', 'DOWNSTREAM', 3))
ORDER BY DISTANCE, DOWNSTREAM_OBJECT;

-- And upstream: where do the agent's answers come from?
SELECT DISTANCE, SOURCE_OBJECT_DOMAIN, SOURCE_OBJECT_DATABASE || '.' || SOURCE_OBJECT_SCHEMA || '.' || SOURCE_OBJECT_NAME AS UPSTREAM_OBJECT
FROM TABLE(SNOWFLAKE.CORE.GET_LINEAGE('BANKING_HOL.AUDIT_PACK.PAYMENTS_AUDIT_AGENT', 'CORTEX_AGENT', 'UPSTREAM', 3))
ORDER BY DISTANCE, UPSTREAM_OBJECT;
-- A row shown as ***.***.*** is an object in the lineage that your role has no
-- privileges on (here the platform team's SEED schema). Lineage never leaks
-- the existence of objects you are not entitled to see.

-- Object dependencies (views, dynamic tables, semantic views) - immediate
SELECT REFERENCING_OBJECT_NAME, REFERENCING_OBJECT_DOMAIN, REFERENCED_OBJECT_NAME
FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES
WHERE REFERENCED_DATABASE = 'BANKING_HOL'
ORDER BY REFERENCED_OBJECT_NAME
LIMIT 50;

-- Make sure there is a restricted-column read to find
SELECT * FROM BANKING_HOL.AUDIT_PACK.CLIENT_ACCOUNTS LIMIT 5;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- GOV2.2 Who accessed restricted columns? (ACCOUNT_USAGE latency applies)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT ah.QUERY_START_TIME, ah.USER_NAME,
       obj.value:objectName::STRING     AS OBJECT_NAME,
       col.value:columnName::STRING     AS COLUMN_NAME
FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ACCESS_HISTORY ah,
     LATERAL FLATTEN(ah.BASE_OBJECTS_ACCESSED) obj,
     LATERAL FLATTEN(obj.value:columns) col
WHERE obj.value:objectName::STRING ILIKE 'BANKING_HOL.%'
  AND col.value:columnName::STRING IN ('IBAN', 'ACCOUNT_NUMBER', 'SORT_CODE')
  AND ah.QUERY_START_TIME >= DATEADD('day', -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
ORDER BY ah.QUERY_START_TIME DESC
LIMIT 20;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- GOV2.3 What are our agents doing? Every agent call is observable
-- Snowsight: AI & ML > Agents > PAYMENTS_AUDIT_AGENT > Monitoring
-- -----------------------------------------------------
SELECT QUERY_TYPE, USER_NAME, ROLE_NAME, START_TIME, TOTAL_ELAPSED_TIME / 1000 AS SECONDS,
       LEFT(QUERY_TEXT, 120) AS QUERY_PREVIEW
FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY
WHERE DATABASE_NAME = 'BANKING_HOL'
  AND QUERY_TEXT ILIKE '%SEMANTIC_VIEW%'
  AND START_TIME >= DATEADD('day', -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
ORDER BY START_TIME DESC
LIMIT 20;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- GOV2.4 Document the data product so humans and AI find the right thing
-- -----------------------------------------------------
COMMENT ON TABLE PAYMENT_SLA_DAILY IS
  'Daily SLA compliance per payment scheme. Owner: Payments Operations. Grain: day x scheme. Source: Iceberg RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS and RAW_DATA.SLA_DEFINITIONS.';
COMMENT ON COLUMN PAYMENT_SLA_DAILY.SLA_STATUS IS
  'COMPLIANT = met success-rate and P95 targets; AT RISK = within 5% of success target; BREACH = otherwise';

-- Ask CoCo:
--   "If I drop column PROCESSING_TIME_MS from BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS,
--    which downstream objects and agents break? Use lineage to check."
--   "Produce a one-page data product card for PAYMENT_SLA_DAILY: owner, grain,
--    lineage, quality checks, sensitivity tags and consumers."

-- In your bank: Trust Center and Horizon Catalog surface the same lineage,
-- classification and access history centrally for the CDO / data office.

SELECT 'GOV2 complete' AS STATUS;

modules.title: AI governance with Cortex AI Gateway
modules.prerequisites: C1 only. Uses the account's Cortex AI Gateway (`SNOWFLAKE`, created by Snowflake)
modules.question: Our teams use coding agents, SDK apps and Snowflake agents. How do we control which models they can reach, see what every request did, and attribute AI spend to each person, without slowing the builders down?
build: Notebook `gov3_ai_gateway` that calls two model families through the gateway and reads back what it recorded
A key pair on your own user, restricted to `HOL_PARTICIPANT` and expiring after a day
A drafted model policy for the gateway (only an account administrator can apply it)
A per-user, per-model view of AI usage from the gateway's traces

steps.title: Open the starter notebook and create its service
steps.body:
1. Open `notebooks/` > **gov3_ai_gateway.ipynb** in the file explorer.
2. In the notebook toolbar, click the arrow next to the status dot (right of the blue run button).
3. Choose **Create new service**.
- Already created one in another module? Pick it under **Select service** instead, usually `USER_SERVICE_1`.
4. Expand **Service settings** and fill in **Connect your notebook** as below. Only the three **bold** rows change.
| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Service name | leave the default (e.g. `USER_SERVICE_1`) |
| Artifact repositories | leave as is (`SNOWFLAKE.SNOWPARK.PYPI_SHARED_REPOSITORY`) |
| Enable distributed compute | off |
| Runtime | leave as is (v3.0 · Python 3.12) |
| Compute type | CPU |
| Custom image | leave empty |
| **Compute pool** | **NOTEBOOK_POOL** (change it from HOL_COMPUTE_POOL_CPU) |
| **Idle timeout** | **1 hour** (change it from 24 hours) |
| **External access integrations** | **HOL_NOTEBOOK_ACCESS_INTEGRATION** (lets notebooks reach Postgres and the AI Gateway; set it here so one service works for every notebook module) |
| Secrets | leave empty |
5. Click **Create and connect**. The first start takes 1-2 minutes.
6. Check the role is **HOL_PARTICIPANT** and the warehouse is **BANKING_WH**, using the role and warehouse button in the notebook toolbar.
**Important:** if you can't see `notebooks/` and `vignettes/`, you're in the wrong Workspace. Pick **banking-hol-pack** from the Workspace dropdown (top left).
The starter notebook has one numbered heading per step, so Cortex Code puts each cell in the right place.
A notebook runs on its own **notebook service**, which you create once with these settings.
steps.where: the **banking-hol-pack** Workspace (not My Workspace) > file explorer > `notebooks/gov3_ai_gateway.ipynb`
steps.expect: the starter notebook open in banking-hol-pack with its numbered headings, and the status dot showing the service connected
steps.mediaCaption: Open the notebook > Create new service > NOTEBOOK_POOL, 1 hour, HOL_NOTEBOOK_ACCESS_INTEGRATION

steps.title: Inspect the gateway
steps.where: the Cortex Code sidebar, with `gov3_ai_gateway` open
steps.prompt: In the open notebook gov3_ai_gateway, put each cell I ask for under its matching numbered heading. Under heading 1, add a SQL cell named gateway that runs SHOW AI GATEWAYS and a SQL cell named gateway_spec that runs DESCRIBE AI GATEWAY SNOWFLAKE. Run them and explain the specification: which models it exposes, whether logging is on, and whether prompts and responses are captured.
steps.expect: one gateway, `SNOWFLAKE`, with its base URL. The specification exposes every model (`name: '*'`) and logs every request's metadata; prompts and responses are **not** captured unless an administrator turns payload capture on.

steps.title: Give yourself a short-lived key
steps.prompt: Add a Python cell named make_key that generates an RSA key pair in memory with the cryptography package and registers the public key on my own user with ALTER USER ADD KEY PAIR GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY PUBLIC_KEY = '<base64 DER public key>' ROLE_RESTRICTION = 'HOL_PARTICIPANT' DAYS_TO_EXPIRY = 1, using get_active_session(). Remove any existing GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY first (REMOVE KEY PAIR has no IF EXISTS, so wrap it in try/except). Keep the private key in a variable called key; never print or save it. Then run SHOW USER KEY PAIRS. Use vignettes/gov3_ai_gateway/gov3_gateway_calls.py in the Workspace as the reference.
steps.expect: `GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY` listed with role restriction `HOL_PARTICIPANT` and an expiry tomorrow. The gateway accepts the same tokens as other Snowflake REST APIs: OAuth, a key-pair JWT or a programmatic access token. A key that's tied to one role and expires in a day can only do what the lab role can, and only today.

steps.title: Call two model families through the gateway
steps.prompt: Add a Python cell named gateway_calls that builds a key-pair JWT from key (issuer ACCOUNT.USER.SHA256:<public key fingerprint>, subject ACCOUNT.USER, 50 minute expiry, signed RS256 with cryptography) and calls the gateway at https://<org>-<account>.snowflakecomputing.com/api/v2/aigateways/snowflake, with underscores in the host replaced by hyphens. Send the header X-Snowflake-Authorization-Token-Type: KEYPAIR_JWT and the conversation header x-snowflake-ai-gateway-conversation-id: gov3-lab. Make two calls with urllib: openai-gpt-5 on /v1/chat/completions asking "In two sentences, why might a CHAPS payment be returned, and what should the operations team check first?", and claude-sonnet-4-5 on /v1/messages asking the same about a delayed SEPA payment. Print each answer and its token usage. Use gov3_gateway_calls.py as the reference.
steps.expect: two answers, one from each model family, each with its token counts. Same endpoint, same credential, two API formats: the gateway routes each request to the right model. Any client that can change its base URL (a coding agent, the OpenAI SDK, an agent framework) could make these calls.

steps.title: See what the gateway recorded
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named my_traces over TABLE(AGENT_TRACE_TABLE('SNOWFLAKE')) for the last hour: one row per trace with the start time, user (resource_attributes:"user"), model (record_attributes:"gen_ai.request.model"), conversation id (record_attributes:"gen_ai.conversation.id"), input and output tokens (record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.input_tokens" and "gen_ai.usage.output_tokens"), duration in milliseconds, and status (http.status_code below 400 is success). Run it and explain the difference between a conversation, a trace and a span.
steps.expect: your two calls, tagged with your user, the model, the `gov3-lab` conversation and their tokens and duration. You see only your own traces: a role with **MONITOR** on the gateway sees everyone's. The same data is charted in Snowsight under **AI & ML > AI Gateway > Observability**.

steps.title: Draft a tighter model policy
steps.prompt: Add a markdown cell explaining the gateway specification, then a code cell (don't run it) with the ALTER AI GATEWAY SNOWFLAKE FROM SPECIFICATION statement an account administrator would run to expose only claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-haiku-4-5 and openai-gpt-5, keep logging on, turn on prompt and response capture, and exclude users tagged BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.PAYLOAD_CAPTURE_EXEMPT from capture. Explain why FROM SPECIFICATION replaces the whole specification, why captured prompts make the trace table sensitive, and how CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST differs from the gateway's model list.
steps.expect: a reviewed specification change, not applied: attendees aren't account administrators, which is the point. The gateway list controls what this door exposes; `CORTEX_MODELS_ALLOWLIST` controls which models anyone in the account can use at all. Capturing prompts helps audit and evaluation but puts customer data into the trace table, so restrict who can read it, and exempt sensitive users.

steps.title: See who is using which model
steps.prompt: Add a SQL cell named usage_by_model over TABLE(AGENT_TRACE_TABLE('SNOWFLAKE')) for the last day: requests, input tokens and output tokens per user and model, plus the failure count. Then add a markdown cell explaining where an AI governance lead gets authoritative credits (SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.AI_GATEWAY_USAGE_HISTORY, which lags), and the controls they can apply: budgets, per-user quotas, and revoking USAGE on the gateway from a role.
steps.expect: your usage by model. Traces show what happened per request; credits come from `AI_GATEWAY_USAGE_HISTORY`, and per-user quotas or a budget stop spend before it surprises you.

modules.check: `gov3_traces` passes once the gateway has recorded at least two of your requests today. Remove your key when you're done: `ALTER USER REMOVE KEY PAIR GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY` (it expires tomorrow anyway).
modules.note: One endpoint, one identity, one trace table for every AI client means the AI governance lead can answer "who used which model, on what, at what cost" from Snowflake alone, and change the policy in one place.
modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- GOV3: AI governance with Cortex AI Gateway - reference SQL
-- The calls themselves are Python (gov3_gateway_calls.py); this is the SQL around them.
-- =====================================================
USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE WAREHOUSE BANKING_WH;

-- 1. The gateway Snowflake created for this account, and its specification
SHOW AI GATEWAYS;
DESCRIBE AI GATEWAY SNOWFLAKE;

-- 2. Your key pair (registered from the notebook with ALTER USER ADD KEY PAIR)
SHOW USER KEY PAIRS;

-- 3. What the gateway recorded for you in the last hour: one row per trace
WITH spans AS (
    SELECT trace:"trace_id"::STRING                                         AS TRACE_ID,
           resource_attributes:"user"::STRING                               AS USER_NAME,
           record_attributes:"gen_ai.request.model"::STRING                 AS MODEL,
           record_attributes:"gen_ai.conversation.id"::STRING               AS CONVERSATION_ID,
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.input_tokens"::STRING)  AS INPUT_TOKENS,
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.output_tokens"::STRING) AS OUTPUT_TOKENS,
           TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"http.status_code"::STRING)      AS HTTP_STATUS,
           start_timestamp, timestamp
    FROM TABLE(AGENT_TRACE_TABLE('SNOWFLAKE'))
    WHERE timestamp >= DATEADD('hour', -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
)
SELECT TRACE_ID, MIN(start_timestamp) AS STARTED_AT, MAX(USER_NAME) AS USER_NAME, MAX(MODEL) AS MODEL,
       MAX(CONVERSATION_ID) AS CONVERSATION_ID, SUM(INPUT_TOKENS) AS INPUT_TOKENS, SUM(OUTPUT_TOKENS) AS OUTPUT_TOKENS,
       DATEDIFF('millisecond', MIN(start_timestamp), MAX(timestamp)) AS DURATION_MS,
       IFF(COUNT_IF(HTTP_STATUS >= 400) = 0, 'SUCCESS', 'FAILURE') AS STATUS
FROM spans
GROUP BY TRACE_ID
ORDER BY STARTED_AT DESC;

-- 4. Draft only: a tighter specification. Needs ACCOUNTADMIN, and FROM SPECIFICATION
--    replaces the whole specification, so start from what DESCRIBE returns.
-- CREATE TAG IF NOT EXISTS BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.PAYLOAD_CAPTURE_EXEMPT;
-- ALTER AI GATEWAY SNOWFLAKE FROM SPECIFICATION $$
-- schema_version: 1
-- models:
--   - name: claude-sonnet-4-5
--   - name: claude-haiku-4-5
--   - name: openai-gpt-5
-- logging:
--   enabled: true
--   capture_payload:
--     request_response: true
--     exclude_tags:
--       - BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.PAYLOAD_CAPTURE_EXEMPT
-- $$;

-- 5. Usage per user and model in the last day (your own rows unless you have MONITOR)
SELECT resource_attributes:"user"::STRING                                       AS USER_NAME,
       record_attributes:"gen_ai.request.model"::STRING                         AS MODEL,
       COUNT(*)                                                                 AS REQUESTS,
       SUM(TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.input_tokens"::STRING))  AS INPUT_TOKENS,
       SUM(TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"gen_ai.usage.output_tokens"::STRING)) AS OUTPUT_TOKENS,
       COUNT_IF(TRY_TO_NUMBER(record_attributes:"http.status_code"::STRING) >= 400) AS FAILURES
FROM TABLE(AGENT_TRACE_TABLE('SNOWFLAKE'))
WHERE timestamp >= DATEADD('day', -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP())
  AND record_attributes:"gen_ai.operation.name"::STRING = 'chat'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY REQUESTS DESC;

-- Authoritative credits (lags; needs Account Usage access):
-- SELECT * FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.AI_GATEWAY_USAGE_HISTORY ORDER BY START_TIME DESC LIMIT 50;

-- 6. Clean up
-- ALTER USER REMOVE KEY PAIR GOV3_GATEWAY_KEY;

modules.title: Answer a customer's data request
modules.prerequisites: GOV1
modules.question: A customer has asked for a copy of everything we hold about them. UK GDPR gives us a month, the search has to be reasonable and proportionate, and financial crime records can't simply be handed over. Can we answer it from the data itself, and prove who has seen it?
build: Copies of the customer tables in `GOVERNANCE`, with a `PERSONAL_DATA` tag on every personal column
Stored procedure `DATA_REQUEST`: everything held about one customer, found from the tags
`DATA_REQUESTS`: each request with its due date, the pack and an AI-drafted cover letter

steps.title: Bring the customer data into GOVERNANCE
steps.prompt: In BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE create table copies (CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE ... AS SELECT *) of these tables from BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA, keeping their names: RB_CUSTOMERS, RB_ACCOUNTS, RB_TRANSACTIONS, RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS, RB_COMPLAINTS, RB_EMAILS, RB_FRAUD_CASES and RB_SAR_NARRATIVES. Show the row count of each.
steps.expect: eight tables; the sources in `RAW_DATA` stay read-only

steps.title: Tag personal data once, by kind
steps.prompt: In BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE create a tag PERSONAL_DATA with allowed values IDENTITY, CONTACT, FINANCIAL, COMMUNICATIONS, FINANCIAL_CRIME. Set it on: RB_CUSTOMERS first name, last name and date of birth (IDENTITY), address line 1 and postcode (CONTACT), annual income and credit score (FINANCIAL); RB_ACCOUNTS product and balance, RB_TRANSACTIONS amount and merchant (FINANCIAL); RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS transcript, RB_COMPLAINTS complaint text, RB_EMAILS body (COMMUNICATIONS); RB_FRAUD_CASES investigator notes and RB_SAR_NARRATIVES narrative (FINANCIAL_CRIME). Then show every tagged column in GOVERNANCE with its value.
steps.expect: 16 tagged columns. From now on, the tags say where personal data lives

steps.title: Find everything about one customer
steps.prompt: In BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE create a table DATA_REQUESTS (REQUEST_ID, CUSTOMER_ID, RECEIVED_AT TIMESTAMP_LTZ, DUE_BY DATE, TABLES_FOUND, ROWS_FOUND, HELD_BACK, LETTER, PACK VARIANT). Then create a Python stored procedure DATA_REQUEST(CUSTOMER VARCHAR) returning VARIANT that: finds every table in GOVERNANCE with a CUSTOMER_ID column and at least one PERSONAL_DATA-tagged column (using INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS and TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS, not a hard-coded list); for each that has rows for the customer, collects the tagged columns (up to 50 rows, bind the customer id); puts any table tagged FINANCIAL_CRIME in a held_back list instead, with only its row count; lists who read those tables in the last 30 days from SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ACCESS_HISTORY (flatten BASE_OBJECTS_ACCESSED in a CTE); drafts a short cover letter with AI_COMPLETE (claude-sonnet-4-5) that never mentions fraud or anything held back; and inserts a DATA_REQUESTS row with DUE_BY one month from today.
steps.expect: one procedure that finds the data from the tags, so a newly tagged table is included automatically

steps.title: Answer the request
steps.prompt: Call BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.DATA_REQUEST('RB101023'), then show the newest row of DATA_REQUESTS: due date, tables found, rows found, how many tables were held back, and the letter.
steps.expect: about 5 tables and 50 records, 2 held back (a fraud case and a SAR), and a due date a month from today

steps.title: Explain what was held back
steps.prompt: For the newest request in BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.DATA_REQUESTS, explain in plain English which records were held back and why a bank would refer financial crime records to its money laundering reporting officer before releasing anything, and what a reviewer should check before the pack goes out.
steps.expect: the reason in plain words, for the person who signs the response off

modules.check: `DATA_REQUESTS` has a row for RB101023 with a due date, the tables found, two held back, and a letter that doesn't mention them.
modules.note: In production the tags sit on the source data products, set by classification, so every copy and pipeline inherits them, and the response goes through the bank's data protection review. The executive demo's "A customer asks for their data" stop is this module, finished.

modules.title: Protect personal data at scale
modules.prerequisites: GOV4 (or `setup/catchup/gov4_tags.sql`, which copies and tags the customer tables)
modules.question: Our customer tables hold names, dates of birth, incomes and complaint text. Analysts need to work with them, model risk needs to see how they are protected, and nobody wants to maintain a masking rule per column. Can we protect every personal column once, by what it is, and prove none is missed?
build: Three masking policies (text, numbers, dates) attached to the `PERSONAL_DATA` tag, so every tagged column is protected by role
`MASKING_COVERAGE`: every personal column with the policy that protects it, and a gap flag
`CUSTOMER_PROTECTED`: a shared customer view that carries the protection to anyone who reads it

steps.title: Check the personal data is tagged
steps.body:
Protection follows the tags, so check GOV4's tags are in place first.
1. Name the file `gov5_protect.sql`, then paste and run:
**Important:** if the query fails or returns 0, GOV4 hasn't been done in this account. Fast-forward instead.
1. In the Lab Companion, find the **Fast-forward** card on this module page.
2. Press **Fast-forward**.
3. Wait for the green tick, then run the query again or press **Check prerequisites**.
steps.where: Snowsight > Projects > Workspaces > + Add new > SQL File, role HOL_PARTICIPANT, warehouse BANKING_WH
steps.expect: 7 tagged columns.

steps.title: Protect each kind of data once
steps.body: One policy per data type, so a new column never needs a new rule. Each policy reads the tag value to decide how much to show.
steps.prompt: In BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE create three masking policies and do not ask me questions. MASK_PD_STRING takes a VARCHAR: HOL_ADMIN sees the real value; HOL_PARTICIPANT sees '[restricted]' when the column's PERSONAL_DATA tag (read with SYSTEM$GET_TAG_ON_CURRENT_COLUMN on BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.PERSONAL_DATA) is FINANCIAL_CRIME, the first character plus '****' for IDENTITY, the first three characters plus '****' for CONTACT, and the real value otherwise; every other role sees '****'. MASK_PD_NUMBER takes a NUMBER: HOL_ADMIN sees the real value; HOL_PARTICIPANT sees it rounded to the nearest 1000 when it is 10000 or more, nearest 10 when it is 100 or more, otherwise to a whole number; every other role sees NULL. MASK_PD_DATE takes a DATE: HOL_ADMIN sees the real value; HOL_PARTICIPANT sees 1 January of the same year; every other role sees NULL. Test the role with CURRENT_ROLE().
steps.expect: three policies in `GOVERNANCE`, none attached yet

steps.title: Attach them to the tag, not to columns
steps.prompt: Attach MASK_PD_STRING, MASK_PD_NUMBER and MASK_PD_DATE to the tag BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.PERSONAL_DATA with ALTER TAG ... SET MASKING POLICY, one statement each. Then grant SELECT on all tables in BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE to the role HOL_RESTRICTED.
steps.expect: every tagged column is protected at once, with no per-column statements

steps.title: See what each person sees
steps.body: **Tip:** run `USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE` before switching role. Otherwise your other roles stay active and nothing looks masked.
steps.prompt: Show 3 rows of BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_CUSTOMERS with FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME, DATE_OF_BIRTH, POSTCODE, ANNUAL_INCOME_GBP and CREDIT_SCORE, first as my current role and then after USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE and USE ROLE HOL_RESTRICTED. Switch back to HOL_PARTICIPANT at the end, and explain the difference.
steps.expect: as the builder, `M****`, a date of 1 January, a postcode cut to three characters and rounded income; as `HOL_RESTRICTED`, `****` and NULLs

steps.title: Prove no personal column is missed
steps.prompt: In BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE create a view MASKING_COVERAGE with one row for every column tagged PERSONAL_DATA in the eight tables RB_CUSTOMERS, RB_ACCOUNTS, RB_TRANSACTIONS, RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS, RB_COMPLAINTS, RB_EMAILS, RB_FRAUD_CASES and RB_SAR_NARRATIVES. Columns: TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, TAG_VALUE, POLICY_NAME and STATUS ('PROTECTED' when a masking policy applies, otherwise 'GAP'). Build it from INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES for each table, then show the count by STATUS.
steps.expect: 16 protected columns and no gaps

steps.title: Tag a new column and see it protected
steps.prompt: In BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_CUSTOMERS set the tag PERSONAL_DATA = 'FINANCIAL' on TOTAL_DEBT_GBP. Without creating any policy, query MASKING_COVERAGE again, then show TOTAL_DEBT_GBP for 3 customers as HOL_RESTRICTED (use USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE first) and switch back to HOL_PARTICIPANT.
steps.expect: 17 protected columns, and `TOTAL_DEBT_GBP` is NULL for `HOL_RESTRICTED`

steps.title: Share a protected data product
steps.prompt: In BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE create a view CUSTOMER_PROTECTED joining RB_CUSTOMERS to RB_ACCOUNTS on CUSTOMER_ID, with CUSTOMER_ID, FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME, DATE_OF_BIRTH, POSTCODE, ANNUAL_INCOME_GBP, CREDIT_SCORE, PRODUCT and BALANCE_GBP. Grant SELECT on it to HOL_RESTRICTED, then show 3 rows as HOL_RESTRICTED (USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE first) and switch back.
steps.expect: the view returns rows, with the policies applied to the underlying columns

modules.check: `MASKING_COVERAGE` shows 17 protected columns and no gaps. `HOL_RESTRICTED` sees `****` and NULLs through `CUSTOMER_PROTECTED`. `HOL_ADMIN` sees real values.
modules.note: Classification sets the `PERSONAL_DATA` tag on the Iceberg source tables, and the three policies are owned by the data governance team. Every copy, view, semantic view and agent then inherits the protection, because Cortex agents run as the user. Network rules and policies, which control where data can be reached from, are set by the platform team and shown on the **Architecture** page.
modules.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- GOV5: Protect personal data at scale (solution / catch-up)
-- One masking policy per data type, attached to the PERSONAL_DATA tag from GOV4, so
-- every tagged column is protected by role: owner sees all, builder sees banded
-- values, everyone else sees nothing. Run as HOL_PARTICIPANT after GOV4.
-- =====================================================
USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE WAREHOUSE BANKING_WH;
USE SCHEMA BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE;

-- 1. One policy per data type, driven by the tag value
CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY MASK_PD_STRING AS (VAL VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() = 'HOL_ADMIN' THEN VAL
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() = 'HOL_PARTICIPANT' THEN
      CASE SYSTEM$GET_TAG_ON_CURRENT_COLUMN('BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.PERSONAL_DATA')
        WHEN 'FINANCIAL_CRIME' THEN '[restricted]'
        WHEN 'IDENTITY' THEN LEFT(VAL, 1) || '****'
        WHEN 'CONTACT'  THEN LEFT(VAL, 3) || '****'
        ELSE VAL
      END
    ELSE '****'
  END;

CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY MASK_PD_NUMBER AS (VAL NUMBER) RETURNS NUMBER ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() = 'HOL_ADMIN' THEN VAL
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() = 'HOL_PARTICIPANT' THEN
      CASE WHEN ABS(VAL) >= 10000 THEN ROUND(VAL, -3) WHEN ABS(VAL) >= 100 THEN ROUND(VAL, -1) ELSE ROUND(VAL, 0) END
    ELSE NULL
  END;

CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY MASK_PD_DATE AS (VAL DATE) RETURNS DATE ->
  CASE
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() = 'HOL_ADMIN' THEN VAL
    WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() = 'HOL_PARTICIPANT' THEN DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', VAL)
    ELSE NULL
  END;

-- 2. Attach them to the tag: every tagged column, now and in future
ALTER TAG PERSONAL_DATA SET MASKING POLICY MASK_PD_STRING;
ALTER TAG PERSONAL_DATA SET MASKING POLICY MASK_PD_NUMBER;
ALTER TAG PERSONAL_DATA SET MASKING POLICY MASK_PD_DATE;

-- 3. Let the restricted role read the tables (it sees masked values only)
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE TO ROLE HOL_RESTRICTED;

-- 4. Prove the coverage: every tagged column and the policy that protects it
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW MASKING_COVERAGE AS
WITH TAGGED AS (
  SELECT OBJECT_NAME AS TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, TAG_VALUE FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS('BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_CUSTOMERS', 'table')) WHERE TAG_NAME = 'PERSONAL_DATA'
  UNION ALL SELECT OBJECT_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, TAG_VALUE FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS('BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_ACCOUNTS', 'table')) WHERE TAG_NAME = 'PERSONAL_DATA'
  UNION ALL SELECT OBJECT_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, TAG_VALUE FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS('BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_TRANSACTIONS', 'table')) WHERE TAG_NAME = 'PERSONAL_DATA'
  UNION ALL SELECT OBJECT_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, TAG_VALUE FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS('BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS', 'table')) WHERE TAG_NAME = 'PERSONAL_DATA'
  UNION ALL SELECT OBJECT_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, TAG_VALUE FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS('BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_COMPLAINTS', 'table')) WHERE TAG_NAME = 'PERSONAL_DATA'
  UNION ALL SELECT OBJECT_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, TAG_VALUE FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS('BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_EMAILS', 'table')) WHERE TAG_NAME = 'PERSONAL_DATA'
  UNION ALL SELECT OBJECT_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, TAG_VALUE FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS('BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_FRAUD_CASES', 'table')) WHERE TAG_NAME = 'PERSONAL_DATA'
  UNION ALL SELECT OBJECT_NAME, COLUMN_NAME, TAG_VALUE FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS('BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_SAR_NARRATIVES', 'table')) WHERE TAG_NAME = 'PERSONAL_DATA'
),
POLICIES AS (
  SELECT 'RB_CUSTOMERS' AS TABLE_NAME, REF_COLUMN_NAME AS COLUMN_NAME, POLICY_NAME FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES(REF_ENTITY_NAME => 'BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_CUSTOMERS', REF_ENTITY_DOMAIN => 'TABLE')) WHERE POLICY_KIND = 'MASKING_POLICY'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'RB_ACCOUNTS', REF_COLUMN_NAME, POLICY_NAME FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES(REF_ENTITY_NAME => 'BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_ACCOUNTS', REF_ENTITY_DOMAIN => 'TABLE')) WHERE POLICY_KIND = 'MASKING_POLICY'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'RB_TRANSACTIONS', REF_COLUMN_NAME, POLICY_NAME FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES(REF_ENTITY_NAME => 'BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_TRANSACTIONS', REF_ENTITY_DOMAIN => 'TABLE')) WHERE POLICY_KIND = 'MASKING_POLICY'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS', REF_COLUMN_NAME, POLICY_NAME FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES(REF_ENTITY_NAME => 'BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_CALL_TRANSCRIPTS', REF_ENTITY_DOMAIN => 'TABLE')) WHERE POLICY_KIND = 'MASKING_POLICY'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'RB_COMPLAINTS', REF_COLUMN_NAME, POLICY_NAME FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES(REF_ENTITY_NAME => 'BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_COMPLAINTS', REF_ENTITY_DOMAIN => 'TABLE')) WHERE POLICY_KIND = 'MASKING_POLICY'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'RB_EMAILS', REF_COLUMN_NAME, POLICY_NAME FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES(REF_ENTITY_NAME => 'BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_EMAILS', REF_ENTITY_DOMAIN => 'TABLE')) WHERE POLICY_KIND = 'MASKING_POLICY'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'RB_FRAUD_CASES', REF_COLUMN_NAME, POLICY_NAME FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES(REF_ENTITY_NAME => 'BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_FRAUD_CASES', REF_ENTITY_DOMAIN => 'TABLE')) WHERE POLICY_KIND = 'MASKING_POLICY'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'RB_SAR_NARRATIVES', REF_COLUMN_NAME, POLICY_NAME FROM TABLE(BANKING_HOL.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.POLICY_REFERENCES(REF_ENTITY_NAME => 'BANKING_HOL.GOVERNANCE.RB_SAR_NARRATIVES', REF_ENTITY_DOMAIN => 'TABLE')) WHERE POLICY_KIND = 'MASKING_POLICY'
)
SELECT T.TABLE_NAME, T.COLUMN_NAME, T.TAG_VALUE, P.POLICY_NAME, IFF(P.POLICY_NAME IS NULL, 'GAP', 'PROTECTED') AS STATUS
FROM TAGGED T LEFT JOIN POLICIES P ON P.TABLE_NAME = T.TABLE_NAME AND P.COLUMN_NAME = T.COLUMN_NAME;

-- 5. A new personal column: tag it and it is protected at once
ALTER TABLE RB_CUSTOMERS MODIFY COLUMN TOTAL_DEBT_GBP SET TAG PERSONAL_DATA = 'FINANCIAL';

-- 6. A protected data product that carries the policies to anyone who reads it
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW CUSTOMER_PROTECTED AS
SELECT C.CUSTOMER_ID, C.FIRST_NAME, C.LAST_NAME, C.DATE_OF_BIRTH, C.POSTCODE, C.ANNUAL_INCOME_GBP, C.CREDIT_SCORE, A.PRODUCT, A.BALANCE_GBP
FROM RB_CUSTOMERS C JOIN RB_ACCOUNTS A ON A.CUSTOMER_ID = C.CUSTOMER_ID;
GRANT SELECT ON VIEW CUSTOMER_PROTECTED TO ROLE HOL_RESTRICTED;

catchups.name: client 360
catchups.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- BANKING HOL PACK - CATCH-UP SCRIPT
-- CLIENT 360 SEMANTIC VIEW (what DA2 builds)
--
-- Run this if you skipped DA2 and your module needs SV_CLIENT_360
-- (OPS1, AI1, AI2, AI3). Safe to re-run.
--   1. Creates the staging views and FEEDBACK_ENRICHED only if they are missing,
--      so it keeps anything DE1 (dbt) or DA1 (AI enrichment) already built.
--      Scoring FEEDBACK_ENRICHED calls AI_SENTIMENT and AI_CLASSIFY once per
--      feedback row (about 2,000 rows).
--   2. Builds DA2's contract views and the semantic view SV_CLIENT_360.
-- Keep sections 1 and 2 in step with core_analytics.sql and da2.sql.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BANKING_WH;
USE SCHEMA BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- =====================================================
-- 1. Analytics layer, only what is missing
-- =====================================================
-- ---------- Staging views ----------
CALL BANKING_HOL.LAB.CATCHUP_STEP(1, 4, 'Building the staging views if they are missing');
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS STG_PAYMENTS AS
SELECT
    PAYMENT_ID,
    PAYMENT_DATE::TIMESTAMP                             AS PAYMENT_DATE,
    DATE_TRUNC('DAY', PAYMENT_DATE::TIMESTAMP)          AS PAYMENT_DAY,
    ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID,
    BENEFICIARY_ACCOUNT_ID,
    UPPER(TRIM(PAYMENT_TYPE))                           AS PAYMENT_TYPE,
    UPPER(TRIM(CHANNEL))                                AS CHANNEL,
    UPPER(TRIM(CURRENCY))                               AS CURRENCY,
    AMOUNT::NUMBER(15,2)                                AS AMOUNT,
    FX_RATE,
    UPPER(TRIM(STATUS))                                 AS STATUS,
    PROCESSING_TIME_MS::NUMBER                          AS PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
    ERROR_CODE,
    UPPER(TRIM(REGION))                                 AS REGION,
    SETTLEMENT_DATE,
    CASE WHEN STATUS = 'COMPLETED' THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END  AS IS_SUCCESSFUL,
    CASE WHEN STATUS = 'FAILED'    THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END  AS IS_FAILED,
    CASE WHEN ERROR_CODE IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS HAS_ERROR
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS STG_FEEDBACK AS
SELECT
    FEEDBACK_ID,
    FEEDBACK_DATE::TIMESTAMP            AS FEEDBACK_DATE,
    DATE_TRUNC('DAY', FEEDBACK_DATE)    AS FEEDBACK_DAY,
    CUSTOMER_ID,
    PAYMENT_ID,
    UPPER(TRIM(FEEDBACK_CHANNEL))       AS FEEDBACK_CHANNEL,
    TRIM(FEEDBACK_TEXT)                 AS FEEDBACK_TEXT,
    UPPER(TRIM(PAYMENT_TYPE))           AS PAYMENT_TYPE,
    RATING::NUMBER(1)                   AS RATING,
    LENGTH(TRIM(FEEDBACK_TEXT))         AS FEEDBACK_LENGTH,
    CASE WHEN RATING >= 4 THEN 'SATISFIED'
         WHEN RATING = 3  THEN 'NEUTRAL'
         ELSE 'DISSATISFIED' END        AS SATISFACTION_TIER
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMER_FEEDBACK
WHERE FEEDBACK_TEXT IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(TRIM(FEEDBACK_TEXT)) > 0;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS STG_CUSTOMERS AS
SELECT
    c.CUSTOMER_ID,
    UPPER(TRIM(c.CUSTOMER_NAME))        AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
    UPPER(TRIM(c.SECTOR))               AS SECTOR,
    c.COUNTRY,
    c.ONBOARDING_DATE,
    UPPER(TRIM(c.KYC_STATUS))           AS KYC_STATUS,
    c.RM_ID,
    r.RM_NAME,
    r.TEAM                              AS RM_TEAM,
    r.REGION                            AS RM_REGION
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS c
LEFT JOIN BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.RELATIONSHIP_MANAGERS r ON c.RM_ID = r.RM_ID;

CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS STG_ACCOUNTS AS
SELECT
    a.ACCOUNT_ID, a.CUSTOMER_ID, a.SORT_CODE, a.ACCOUNT_NUMBER, a.IBAN, a.BIC,
    UPPER(TRIM(a.CURRENCY))             AS CURRENCY,
    UPPER(TRIM(a.ACCOUNT_TYPE))         AS ACCOUNT_TYPE,
    UPPER(TRIM(a.STATUS))               AS STATUS,
    a.OPENED_DATE,
    c.CUSTOMER_NAME,
    c.SECTOR                            AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.ACCOUNTS a
LEFT JOIN BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID;

-- ---------- AI enrichment (skipped if DA1 or core_analytics.sql already built it) ----------
CALL BANKING_HOL.LAB.CATCHUP_STEP(2, 4, 'Scoring customer feedback with AI if it is missing');
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS FEEDBACK_ENRICHED AS
WITH ai_scored AS (
    SELECT f.*, c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.SECTOR AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR, c.RM_NAME,
           -- AI_SENTIMENT returns a label, so map the overall label to -1, 0 or 1
           -- (legacy SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SENTIMENT is blocked on new accounts)
           DECODE(GET(FILTER(AI_SENTIMENT(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT):categories, c -> c:name::STRING = 'overall'), 0):sentiment::STRING,
                  'positive', 1, 'negative', -1, 0)::FLOAT AS SENTIMENT_SCORE,
           AI_CLASSIFY(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT,
               ['Performance Issue','Service Quality','Technical Problem',
                'Positive Experience','Feature Request']) AS CLASSIFICATION_RESULT
    FROM STG_FEEDBACK f
    LEFT JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON f.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
)
SELECT FEEDBACK_ID, FEEDBACK_DATE, CUSTOMER_ID, CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, RM_NAME,
       PAYMENT_ID, FEEDBACK_CHANNEL, FEEDBACK_TEXT, PAYMENT_TYPE, RATING, SENTIMENT_SCORE,
       CASE WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE >  0.3 THEN 'POSITIVE'
            WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE < -0.3 THEN 'NEGATIVE'
            ELSE 'NEUTRAL' END                      AS SENTIMENT_LABEL,
       CLASSIFICATION_RESULT:labels[0]::STRING      AS TOPIC_CATEGORY
FROM ai_scored;

-- =====================================================
-- 2. DA2: contract views and SV_CLIENT_360
-- =====================================================
-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.1 Stable interface views (semantic views should sit on contracts, not raw)
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CALL BANKING_HOL.LAB.CATCHUP_STEP(3, 4, 'Building the client summary views');
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY
    COMMENT = 'One row per corporate client: payment volumes, success and latency'
AS
SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID,
       COUNT(*)                                                     AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
       COUNT_IF(p.IS_SUCCESSFUL)                                    AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
       COUNT_IF(p.IS_FAILED)                                        AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
       SUM(p.AMOUNT)                                                AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
       SUM(IFF(p.IS_FAILED, p.AMOUNT, 0))                           AS FAILED_VOLUME_GBP,
       ROUND(AVG(p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS), 0)                          AS AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
       MAX(p.PAYMENT_DATE)                                          AS LAST_PAYMENT_DATE
FROM STG_PAYMENTS p
JOIN STG_ACCOUNTS  a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_ID;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW V_CLIENT_ALERTS
    COMMENT = 'Operational alerts attributed to the originating corporate client'
AS
SELECT al.ALERT_ID, a.CUSTOMER_ID, al.ALERT_TIME::TIMESTAMP AS ALERT_TIME,
       al.SEVERITY, al.PAYMENT_TYPE, al.STATUS AS ALERT_STATUS,
       al.ASSIGNED_TO, al.RESOLUTION_TIME_MIN, al.ALERT_DESCRIPTION
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.OPERATIONAL_ALERTS al
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS p ON al.PAYMENT_ID = p.PAYMENT_ID
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.ACCOUNTS a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID;

-- -----------------------------------------------------
-- DA2.2 The semantic view: business names, relationships, metrics, synonyms
-- Tip: you can also build this in Snowsight (AI & ML > Cortex Analyst > Create)
-- or ask CoCo: "Create a semantic view over STG_CUSTOMERS, V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY,
-- FEEDBACK_ENRICHED and V_CLIENT_ALERTS joined on CUSTOMER_ID."
-- -----------------------------------------------------
CALL BANKING_HOL.LAB.CATCHUP_STEP(4, 4, 'Creating the SV_CLIENT_360 semantic view');
CREATE OR REPLACE SEMANTIC VIEW SV_CLIENT_360

  TABLES (
    clients AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS
      PRIMARY KEY (CUSTOMER_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('customers', 'corporate clients', 'accounts')
      COMMENT = 'Corporate banking clients with KYC status and assigned relationship manager',
    payments AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY
      PRIMARY KEY (CUSTOMER_ID)
      COMMENT = 'Payment activity summary per client',
    feedback AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED
      PRIMARY KEY (FEEDBACK_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('complaints', 'customer feedback', 'sentiment')
      COMMENT = 'Client feedback with AI sentiment and topic',
    alerts AS BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_ALERTS
      PRIMARY KEY (ALERT_ID)
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('incidents', 'operational alerts')
      COMMENT = 'Operational payment alerts per client'
  )

  RELATIONSHIPS (
    payments_to_clients AS payments (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES clients,
    feedback_to_clients AS feedback (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES clients,
    alerts_to_clients   AS alerts   (CUSTOMER_ID) REFERENCES clients
  )

  FACTS (
    payments.total_payments      AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
    payments.successful_payments AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
    payments.failed_payments     AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
    payments.total_volume_gbp    AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
    payments.failed_volume_gbp   AS FAILED_VOLUME_GBP,
    feedback.sentiment_score     AS SENTIMENT_SCORE,
    feedback.rating              AS RATING,
    alerts.resolution_time_min   AS RESOLUTION_TIME_MIN
  )

  DIMENSIONS (
    clients.customer_name AS CUSTOMER_NAME
      WITH SYNONYMS = ('client', 'client name', 'company')
      COMMENT = 'Registered legal entity name (upper case)',
    clients.sector        AS SECTOR WITH SYNONYMS = ('industry'),
    clients.country       AS COUNTRY COMMENT = 'ISO alpha-3 country code',
    clients.kyc_status    AS KYC_STATUS COMMENT = 'APPROVED, PENDING_REVIEW, EXPIRED',
    clients.rm_name       AS RM_NAME WITH SYNONYMS = ('relationship manager', 'RM', 'banker'),
    clients.rm_team       AS RM_TEAM COMMENT = 'Corporate, Institutional or SME banking team',
    feedback.sentiment_label AS SENTIMENT_LABEL COMMENT = 'POSITIVE, NEUTRAL, NEGATIVE',
    feedback.topic_category  AS TOPIC_CATEGORY,
    feedback.feedback_payment_type AS PAYMENT_TYPE COMMENT = 'Payment scheme the feedback refers to',
    feedback.feedback_date   AS FEEDBACK_DATE,
    alerts.severity       AS SEVERITY COMMENT = 'LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL',
    alerts.alert_status   AS ALERT_STATUS COMMENT = 'OPEN, ACKNOWLEDGED, INVESTIGATING, RESOLVED',
    alerts.alert_time     AS ALERT_TIME
  )

  METRICS (
    payments.payment_count     AS SUM(payments.total_payments) WITH SYNONYMS = ('number of payments'),
    payments.payment_volume    AS SUM(payments.total_volume_gbp) WITH SYNONYMS = ('volume', 'value'),
    payments.failed_volume     AS SUM(payments.failed_volume_gbp) WITH SYNONYMS = ('value at risk'),
    payments.success_rate_pct  AS ROUND(SUM(payments.successful_payments) / NULLIF(SUM(payments.total_payments), 0) * 100, 2)
      COMMENT = 'Weighted payment success rate %',
    feedback.avg_sentiment     AS ROUND(AVG(feedback.sentiment_score), 3),
    feedback.negative_feedback_count AS COUNT_IF(feedback.sentiment_label = 'NEGATIVE'),
    alerts.open_alert_count    AS COUNT_IF(alerts.alert_status <> 'RESOLVED') WITH SYNONYMS = ('open incidents'),
    alerts.critical_alert_count AS COUNT_IF(alerts.severity = 'CRITICAL'),
    alerts.avg_resolution_min  AS ROUND(AVG(alerts.resolution_time_min), 0)
  )

  COMMENT = 'Corporate Client 360 for Payments Operations: payments health, feedback sentiment and operational alerts per client'

  AI_SQL_GENERATION 'Sentiment labels are stored in upper case: POSITIVE, NEUTRAL or NEGATIVE. "Negative sentiment" for a client means their average sentiment score is below 0. Client names are stored in upper case; match them case-insensitively with ILIKE. Round percentages to 1 decimal place.'

  AI_VERIFIED_QUERIES (
    worst_clients AS (
      QUESTION 'Which 5 clients have the lowest payment success rate?'
      ONBOARDING_QUESTION TRUE
      SQL 'SELECT c.CUSTOMER_NAME, ROUND(SUM(p.SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS) / NULLIF(SUM(p.TOTAL_PAYMENTS), 0) * 100, 2) AS success_rate_pct
           FROM BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY p
           JOIN BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON p.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
           GROUP BY c.CUSTOMER_NAME ORDER BY success_rate_pct ASC LIMIT 5'
    ),
    rm_open_alerts AS (
      QUESTION 'How many open alerts does each relationship manager have across their clients?'
      ONBOARDING_QUESTION TRUE
      SQL 'SELECT c.RM_NAME, COUNT_IF(a.ALERT_STATUS <> ''RESOLVED'') AS open_alerts
           FROM BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_ALERTS a
           JOIN BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
           GROUP BY c.RM_NAME ORDER BY open_alerts DESC'
    ),
    negative_sentiment_low_success AS (
      QUESTION 'Which clients have negative sentiment and a success rate below 96%?'
      SQL 'WITH s AS (SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, AVG(SENTIMENT_SCORE) AS avg_sentiment
                     FROM BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.FEEDBACK_ENRICHED GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID)
           SELECT c.CUSTOMER_NAME, ROUND(s.avg_sentiment, 3) AS avg_sentiment,
                  ROUND(p.SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS / NULLIF(p.TOTAL_PAYMENTS, 0) * 100, 1) AS success_rate_pct
           FROM BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY p
           JOIN BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS.STG_CUSTOMERS c ON p.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
           JOIN s ON s.CUSTOMER_ID = p.CUSTOMER_ID
           WHERE s.avg_sentiment < 0 AND p.SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS / NULLIF(p.TOTAL_PAYMENTS, 0) * 100 < 96
           ORDER BY success_rate_pct'
    )
  );

SELECT 'Client 360 catch-up complete' AS STATUS,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM V_CLIENT_PAYMENT_SUMMARY) AS CLIENTS,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED)        AS FEEDBACK_ROWS;

catchups.name: core analytics
catchups.sql:
-- =====================================================
-- BANKING HOL PACK - CATCH-UP SCRIPT
-- CORE ANALYTICS LAYER (pure SQL equivalent of the dbt project + AI enrichment)
--
-- Run this if your chosen vignette needs the analytics layer and you have
-- not completed DE1 (dbt) / DA1 (AI enrichment). Safe to re-run.
-- Objects match dbt/models exactly so later vignettes behave the same.
-- =====================================================

USE ROLE HOL_PARTICIPANT;
USE SECONDARY ROLES NONE;   -- see exactly what an attendee sees
USE WAREHOUSE BANKING_WH;
USE SCHEMA BANKING_HOL.ANALYTICS;

-- ---------- Staging views ----------
CALL BANKING_HOL.LAB.CATCHUP_STEP(1, 3, 'Building the staging views');
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STG_PAYMENTS AS
SELECT
    PAYMENT_ID,
    PAYMENT_DATE::TIMESTAMP                             AS PAYMENT_DATE,
    DATE_TRUNC('DAY', PAYMENT_DATE::TIMESTAMP)          AS PAYMENT_DAY,
    ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID,
    BENEFICIARY_ACCOUNT_ID,
    UPPER(TRIM(PAYMENT_TYPE))                           AS PAYMENT_TYPE,
    UPPER(TRIM(CHANNEL))                                AS CHANNEL,
    UPPER(TRIM(CURRENCY))                               AS CURRENCY,
    AMOUNT::NUMBER(15,2)                                AS AMOUNT,
    FX_RATE,
    UPPER(TRIM(STATUS))                                 AS STATUS,
    PROCESSING_TIME_MS::NUMBER                          AS PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
    ERROR_CODE,
    UPPER(TRIM(REGION))                                 AS REGION,
    SETTLEMENT_DATE,
    CASE WHEN STATUS = 'COMPLETED' THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END  AS IS_SUCCESSFUL,
    CASE WHEN STATUS = 'FAILED'    THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END  AS IS_FAILED,
    CASE WHEN ERROR_CODE IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS HAS_ERROR
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.PAYMENTS;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STG_FEEDBACK AS
SELECT
    FEEDBACK_ID,
    FEEDBACK_DATE::TIMESTAMP            AS FEEDBACK_DATE,
    DATE_TRUNC('DAY', FEEDBACK_DATE)    AS FEEDBACK_DAY,
    CUSTOMER_ID,
    PAYMENT_ID,
    UPPER(TRIM(FEEDBACK_CHANNEL))       AS FEEDBACK_CHANNEL,
    TRIM(FEEDBACK_TEXT)                 AS FEEDBACK_TEXT,
    UPPER(TRIM(PAYMENT_TYPE))           AS PAYMENT_TYPE,
    RATING::NUMBER(1)                   AS RATING,
    LENGTH(TRIM(FEEDBACK_TEXT))         AS FEEDBACK_LENGTH,
    CASE WHEN RATING >= 4 THEN 'SATISFIED'
         WHEN RATING = 3  THEN 'NEUTRAL'
         ELSE 'DISSATISFIED' END        AS SATISFACTION_TIER
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMER_FEEDBACK
WHERE FEEDBACK_TEXT IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(TRIM(FEEDBACK_TEXT)) > 0;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STG_CUSTOMERS AS
SELECT
    c.CUSTOMER_ID,
    UPPER(TRIM(c.CUSTOMER_NAME))        AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
    UPPER(TRIM(c.SECTOR))               AS SECTOR,
    c.COUNTRY,
    c.ONBOARDING_DATE,
    UPPER(TRIM(c.KYC_STATUS))           AS KYC_STATUS,
    c.RM_ID,
    r.RM_NAME,
    r.TEAM                              AS RM_TEAM,
    r.REGION                            AS RM_REGION
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS c
LEFT JOIN BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.RELATIONSHIP_MANAGERS r ON c.RM_ID = r.RM_ID;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW STG_ACCOUNTS AS
SELECT
    a.ACCOUNT_ID, a.CUSTOMER_ID, a.SORT_CODE, a.ACCOUNT_NUMBER, a.IBAN, a.BIC,
    UPPER(TRIM(a.CURRENCY))             AS CURRENCY,
    UPPER(TRIM(a.ACCOUNT_TYPE))         AS ACCOUNT_TYPE,
    UPPER(TRIM(a.STATUS))               AS STATUS,
    a.OPENED_DATE,
    c.CUSTOMER_NAME,
    c.SECTOR                            AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR
FROM BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.ACCOUNTS a
LEFT JOIN BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID;

-- ---------- Marts ----------
CALL BANKING_HOL.LAB.CATCHUP_STEP(2, 3, 'Building the payment, SLA and customer marts');
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE MART_PAYMENT_KPIS AS
SELECT
    p.PAYMENT_DAY, p.PAYMENT_TYPE, p.REGION, p.CHANNEL,
    c.SECTOR AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR, c.RM_NAME, c.RM_TEAM,
    COUNT(*)                                                   AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
    SUM(p.AMOUNT)                                              AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
    ROUND(AVG(p.AMOUNT), 2)                                    AS AVG_PAYMENT_AMOUNT,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN p.IS_SUCCESSFUL THEN 1 END)                AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN p.IS_FAILED     THEN 1 END)                AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
    ROUND(COUNT(CASE WHEN p.IS_SUCCESSFUL THEN 1 END)::FLOAT / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) * 100, 2) AS SUCCESS_RATE_PCT,
    ROUND(AVG(p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS), 0)                        AS AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS), 0) AS P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS
FROM STG_PAYMENTS p
LEFT JOIN STG_ACCOUNTS  a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
LEFT JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
GROUP BY p.PAYMENT_DAY, p.PAYMENT_TYPE, p.REGION, p.CHANNEL, c.SECTOR, c.RM_NAME, c.RM_TEAM;

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE AS
WITH daily_scheme AS (
    SELECT PAYMENT_DAY, PAYMENT_TYPE,
           SUM(TOTAL_PAYMENTS) AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
           SUM(SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS) AS SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS,
           SUM(FAILED_PAYMENTS) AS FAILED_PAYMENTS,
           ROUND(SUM(SUCCESSFUL_PAYMENTS)::FLOAT / NULLIF(SUM(TOTAL_PAYMENTS), 0) * 100, 2) AS SUCCESS_RATE_PCT,
           MAX(P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS) AS P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS
    FROM MART_PAYMENT_KPIS
    GROUP BY PAYMENT_DAY, PAYMENT_TYPE
)
SELECT
    d.PAYMENT_DAY, d.PAYMENT_TYPE, s.SLA_NAME,
    s.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE    AS SLA_TARGET_PCT,
    s.MAX_PROCESSING_TIME_MS AS SLA_THRESHOLD_MS,
    d.SUCCESS_RATE_PCT       AS ACTUAL_SUCCESS_RATE,
    d.P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS AS ACTUAL_P95_MS,
    d.TOTAL_PAYMENTS, d.FAILED_PAYMENTS,
    CASE WHEN d.SUCCESS_RATE_PCT >= s.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE
           AND d.P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS <= s.MAX_PROCESSING_TIME_MS THEN 'COMPLIANT'
         WHEN d.SUCCESS_RATE_PCT >= s.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE * 0.95 THEN 'AT RISK'
         ELSE 'BREACH' END   AS SLA_STATUS,
    ROUND(d.SUCCESS_RATE_PCT - s.TARGET_SUCCESS_RATE, 2) AS RATE_GAP_PCT,
    d.P95_PROCESSING_TIME_MS - s.MAX_PROCESSING_TIME_MS  AS TIME_GAP_MS
FROM daily_scheme d
JOIN BANKING_HOL.RAW_DATA.SLA_DEFINITIONS s ON d.PAYMENT_TYPE = s.PAYMENT_TYPE;

-- CoCo-built marts from the original lab (DE1 step 3), pre-built here
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE MART_CUSTOMER_PAYMENTS AS
WITH base AS (
    SELECT c.CUSTOMER_ID, c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.SECTOR AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR, c.RM_NAME,
           p.PAYMENT_TYPE, p.AMOUNT, p.IS_SUCCESSFUL, p.PROCESSING_TIME_MS
    FROM STG_PAYMENTS p
    JOIN STG_ACCOUNTS  a ON p.ORIGINATOR_ACCOUNT_ID = a.ACCOUNT_ID
    JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON a.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
), top_scheme AS (
    SELECT CUSTOMER_ID, PAYMENT_TYPE AS MOST_USED_SCHEME
    FROM base GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID, PAYMENT_TYPE
    QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY CUSTOMER_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) = 1
)
SELECT b.CUSTOMER_ID, b.CUSTOMER_NAME, b.CUSTOMER_SECTOR, b.RM_NAME,
       COUNT(*)                                                   AS TOTAL_PAYMENTS,
       SUM(b.AMOUNT)                                              AS TOTAL_VOLUME_GBP,
       ROUND(COUNT_IF(b.IS_SUCCESSFUL)::FLOAT / COUNT(*) * 100, 2) AS SUCCESS_RATE_PCT,
       ROUND(AVG(b.PROCESSING_TIME_MS), 0)                        AS AVG_PROCESSING_TIME_MS,
       t.MOST_USED_SCHEME
FROM base b JOIN top_scheme t USING (CUSTOMER_ID)
GROUP BY b.CUSTOMER_ID, b.CUSTOMER_NAME, b.CUSTOMER_SECTOR, b.RM_NAME, t.MOST_USED_SCHEME;

-- ---------- AI enrichment (DA1 builds this step by step) ----------
CALL BANKING_HOL.LAB.CATCHUP_STEP(3, 3, 'Scoring customer feedback with AI (the longest step)');
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FEEDBACK_ENRICHED AS
WITH ai_scored AS (
    SELECT f.*, c.CUSTOMER_NAME, c.SECTOR AS CUSTOMER_SECTOR, c.RM_NAME,
           -- AI_SENTIMENT returns a label, so map the overall label to -1, 0 or 1
           -- (legacy SNOWFLAKE.CORTEX.SENTIMENT is blocked on new accounts)
           DECODE(GET(FILTER(AI_SENTIMENT(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT):categories, c -> c:name::STRING = 'overall'), 0):sentiment::STRING,
                  'positive', 1, 'negative', -1, 0)::FLOAT AS SENTIMENT_SCORE,
           AI_CLASSIFY(f.FEEDBACK_TEXT,
               ['Performance Issue','Service Quality','Technical Problem',
                'Positive Experience','Feature Request']) AS CLASSIFICATION_RESULT
    FROM STG_FEEDBACK f
    LEFT JOIN STG_CUSTOMERS c ON f.CUSTOMER_ID = c.CUSTOMER_ID
)
SELECT FEEDBACK_ID, FEEDBACK_DATE, CUSTOMER_ID, CUSTOMER_NAME, CUSTOMER_SECTOR, RM_NAME,
       PAYMENT_ID, FEEDBACK_CHANNEL, FEEDBACK_TEXT, PAYMENT_TYPE, RATING, SENTIMENT_SCORE,
       CASE WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE >  0.3 THEN 'POSITIVE'
            WHEN SENTIMENT_SCORE < -0.3 THEN 'NEGATIVE'
            ELSE 'NEUTRAL' END                      AS SENTIMENT_LABEL,
       CLASSIFICATION_RESULT:labels[0]::STRING      AS TOPIC_CATEGORY
FROM ai_scored;

SELECT 'Core analytics catch-up complete' AS STATUS,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM MART_PAYMENT_KPIS)   AS KPI_ROWS,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM MART_SLA_COMPLIANCE) AS SLA_ROWS,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM FEEDBACK_ENRICHED)   AS FEEDBACK_ROWS;

architecture.intro: A guided look at the end state everyone will be building towards, so each pathway knows where its work fits.

points.title: Iceberg is the contract
points.body: Source data arrives centrally as Iceberg, so the same files can be read by other engines. Attendees cannot load or change it, and that is deliberate.

points.title: Build data products, not copies
points.body: Everything downstream is a view, dynamic table or mart. DE1 publishes a mart back out as Iceberg.

points.title: A semantic view is the trust layer for AI
points.body: Business definitions (success rate, value at risk, open alerts) live in one place. Analyst, agents and MCP clients all use it.

points.title: Adopt at your own pace
points.body: Each capability is a separate module, so you can switch on what your organisation has approved and leave the rest. AI3 answers from a Marketplace knowledge extension, and AI5 shows Cortex Search over your own data.

points.title: Governance follows the data
points.body: Policies on the source flow through every model, view and agent, because agents run as the user.
